title: Measurement- And Feedback-Driven Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, And Dapeng Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, and Dapeng Yu

Midcircuit measurements and feedback operations conditioned on the measurement outcomes are essential for implementing quantum error-correction on quantum hardware. When integrated in quantum many-body dynamics, they can give rise to novel nonequilibrium phase transitions both at the level of each i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010401] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates measurement- and feedback-driven nonequilibrium phase transitions on a quantum processor, revealing novel steady-state phases and transitions.
motivation: Midcircuit measurements and feedback are crucial for quantum error correction, but their integration into many-body dynamics can induce novel nonequilibrium phase transitions that are not yet well understood.
method: Using a superconducting quantum processor, the authors implement a protocol with repeated measurements and conditional feedback on a chain of qubits, and characterize the resulting steady states via correlation functions and entanglement measures.
result: They observe multiple nonequilibrium phases, including a 'measurement-induced' phase transition and a feedback-induced transition, with distinct entanglement and correlation properties.
conclusion: The work establishes a new class of nonequilibrium phase transitions driven by measurement and feedback, with implications for quantum control and error correction.

title: Observation And Modulation Of The Quantum Mpemba Effect On A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yueshan Xu et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Yueshan Xu et al.

Observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010402] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has quantum analogs that challenge our understanding of non-equilibrium thermodynamics. Observing and controlling this effect in a quantum platform provides insights into quantum thermalization and information dynamics.
method: Using an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor, the authors prepare initial states with different temperatures and monitor their relaxation dynamics under controlled dissipation.
result: They observe the quantum Mpemba effect, where initially hotter states thermalize faster than colder ones, and demonstrate modulation of the effect by tuning system parameters.
conclusion: The work establishes a controllable quantum platform to study anomalous thermalization, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Bundling Of Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Maike Drieb-Schön, Florian Dreier, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Maike Drieb-Schön, Florian Dreier, and Wolfgang Lechner

We investigate bipartite entanglement and prove that in constrained energy subspaces, the entanglement spectra of multiple bipartitions are the same across the whole subspace. We show that in quantum many-body systems the bipartite entanglement entropy is affected in such a way that it forms “bundle…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that in constrained energy subspaces, entanglement spectra of multiple bipartitions are identical, leading to 'bundles' of bipartite entanglement in many-body systems.
motivation: Understanding entanglement structure in many-body systems is crucial for quantum information processing; the paper aims to characterize bipartite entanglement under energy constraints.
method: The authors use analytical proofs based on entanglement spectrum analysis and symmetry arguments to show that within a constrained energy subspace, all bipartitions share the same entanglement spectrum.
result: They demonstrate that bipartite entanglement entropy forms bundles, meaning that the entanglement across different cuts is identical within the subspace, which has implications for entanglement scaling and area laws.
conclusion: The work reveals a new structural property of entanglement in many-body systems, potentially simplifying the description of entanglement in constrained settings and aiding in quantum simulation and error correction.

title: Quantifying And Probing Multipartite Entanglement Via Minimum Entanglement Drop
authors: Dong-Dong Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Dong Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, and Dong Wang

Quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement remains a significant challenge due to the exponential scaling of computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a multipartite entanglement monotone defined by the minimum entanglement drop—the reduction in global one-to-group entanglement when a s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012402] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a multipartite entanglement monotone based on minimum entanglement drop to quantify genuine multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging due to exponential complexity; existing measures are often difficult to compute or not monotonic.
method: Defines the minimum entanglement drop as the reduction in global one-to-group entanglement when a subsystem is discarded, and proves it is an entanglement monotone under LOCC.
result: The measure is shown to be a valid entanglement monotone, computable for certain classes of states, and capable of detecting genuine multipartite entanglement.
conclusion: The minimum entanglement drop provides a practical and theoretically sound tool for quantifying multipartite entanglement, advancing entanglement theory.

title: Quantitative And Optimal Device-independent Lower Bounds On Detection Efficiency
authors: Arkaprabha Ghosal, Soumyadip Patra, And Peter Bierhorst
abstract:
Author(s): Arkaprabha Ghosal, Soumyadip Patra, and Peter Bierhorst

The authors establish a quantitative and optimal lower bound on detector efficiency in a (2,2,2) Bell experiment within a device-independent framework. They provide a tight lower bound on the minimum efficiency required to observe a desired Bell-CHSH violation using the Navascués-Pironio-Acín hierarchy.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012404] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes quantitative and optimal lower bounds on detector efficiency for Bell-CHSH violation in a device-independent framework using the NPA hierarchy.
motivation: Device-independent protocols rely on Bell inequality violations, which require detectors with sufficient efficiency; a tight lower bound on this efficiency is crucial for practical implementations.
method: Uses the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy to derive a tight lower bound on the minimum detection efficiency needed to achieve a given Bell-CHSH violation in a (2,2,2) Bell experiment.
result: Provides a quantitative and optimal lower bound on detector efficiency, showing the minimum efficiency required to observe a desired Bell-CHSH violation.
conclusion: The bound is tight and optimal, offering a fundamental limit for device-independent quantum information protocols relying on Bell tests.

title: Direct Temperature Inference In Nonequilibrium Quantum Thermometry
authors: Yan Xie And Junjie Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Xie and Junjie Liu

Quantum thermometry aims to measure temperature in nanoscale quantum systems, paralleling classical thermometry. Nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, emerging as a complement to its equilibrium counterpart, addresses scenarios where thermalization is prohibitively slow or real-time temperature monito…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062226] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a direct temperature inference method for nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, addressing scenarios where thermalization is slow.
motivation: Traditional equilibrium thermometry fails when thermalization is slow or real-time monitoring is needed; nonequilibrium quantum thermometry offers a solution but requires efficient temperature inference.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework that directly infers temperature from nonequilibrium measurements, likely using quantum probes and exploiting fluctuation relations or information-theoretic bounds.
result: The method provides accurate temperature estimates in nonequilibrium settings, with potential advantages in speed and precision over equilibrium approaches.
conclusion: Direct temperature inference in nonequilibrium quantum thermometry is feasible and opens new avenues for nanoscale temperature sensing.

title: Entanglement Entropy From Correlation Functions Of Scalar Fields In And Out Of Equilibrium
authors: Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, And Rajdeep Sensarma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, and Rajdeep Sensarma

We show that odd order Rényi entropies [MATH] of a system of interacting scalar fields can be calculated as the free energy of [MATH] replicas of the system with additional quadratic inter-replica couplings in the subsystem at the time of measurement of the entropy. These couplings replace b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062463] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that odd-order Rényi entropies of interacting scalar fields can be computed as the free energy of replicas with quadratic inter-replica couplings, enabling calculation from correlation functions.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a key measure in quantum information and many-body physics, but its calculation for interacting quantum fields is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical method to compute Rényi entropies from correlation functions.
method: The authors derive a replica trick for odd-order Rényi entropies, mapping the entropy to the free energy of a system of replicas with additional quadratic couplings within the subsystem. They then use functional integral techniques to relate this to correlation functions.
result: They obtain explicit formulas for the Rényi entropy in terms of the Green's functions of the original and replica systems, and demonstrate the method for a free scalar field and a scalar field with quartic interaction in and out of equilibrium.
conclusion: The method provides a practical way to compute entanglement entropy from correlation functions, applicable to both equilibrium and non-equilibrium settings, and can be extended to other quantum field theories.

title: Generalized Jarzynski Inequalities For Dissipative And Field-theoretic Systems
authors: Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos And Petr Jizba
abstract:
Author(s): Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos and Petr Jizba

The Jarzynski equality, which relates equilibrium free-energy difference to an average of nonequilibrium work, plays a central role in modern nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics. In this paper we study a weaker consequence of this relation, known as Jarzynski's inequality, which can be formall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes Jarzynski's inequality to dissipative and field-theoretic systems, providing a weaker but more broadly applicable bound on free energy differences.
motivation: The Jarzynski equality is powerful but requires detailed work distributions; a simpler inequality could be more practical for complex systems.
method: The authors derive generalized Jarzynski inequalities using the concept of relative entropy and apply them to dissipative systems and field theories.
result: They obtain inequalities that hold under weaker conditions than the original equality, and demonstrate their validity in specific examples.
conclusion: The generalized inequalities extend the applicability of fluctuation theorems to a wider class of nonequilibrium processes.

title: Thermodynamic Length In Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Far-from-equilibrium Systems: Unification Of Fluctuation Relation And Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

The Boltzmann distribution for an equilibrium system constrains the statistics of the system by the energetics. Despite the nonequilibrium generalization of the Boltzmann distribution being studied extensively, a unified framework valid for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking. Her…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014103] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper unifies fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations in far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems using the concept of thermodynamic length.
motivation: A unified framework for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking, despite extensive study of nonequilibrium generalizations of the Boltzmann distribution.
method: The authors derive a thermodynamic length that connects fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations, providing a geometric perspective on nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
result: They show that the thermodynamic length quantifies the trade-off between dissipation and precision, unifying two key results in stochastic thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of far-from-equilibrium thermodynamics and offers a unified tool for analyzing discrete-state systems.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, providing a full counting statistics approach to characterize thermodynamic quantities.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic processes in quantum systems is crucial for developing nanoscale heat engines, where quantum effects play a significant role.
method: The authors use a full counting statistics framework to compute the distributions of heat and work for a driven quantum resonator, incorporating quantum fluctuations.
result: They derive explicit expressions for the heat and work distributions and show that the resonator exhibits nonclassical features such as negative work fluctuations.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive thermodynamic analysis of a quantum resonator, highlighting the impact of quantum coherence on energy exchange and fluctuations.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for Petz f-divergences, linking distinguishability to quadratic contrasts.
motivation: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations (TURs) bound fluctuations in thermodynamic processes; extending them to quantum f-divergences provides a unified framework for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The author shows that any Petz f-divergence can be expressed as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts, using operator convex functions and spectral decomposition.
result: A universal TUR is obtained that holds for any operator convex function, generalizing previous results and providing tight bounds on distinguishability.
conclusion: This work establishes a fundamental link between quantum information measures and thermodynamic constraints, with implications for quantum heat engines and fluctuation theorems.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks using directional coupling.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, and nonreciprocal elements offer a way to control the flow of quantum correlations.
method: The authors model a continuous-variable quantum network with directional couplers and analyze entanglement transport using covariance matrix formalism.
result: They identify a regime where entanglement is efficiently transmitted and show that excess excitations from strong squeezing limit the mechanism.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal coupling enables controlled entanglement routing, but practical implementation must manage squeezing-induced noise.

title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer
abstract:
Author(s): Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, and Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system of a superconducting transmon qubit, a coplanar-waveguide resonator, and an NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting qubits with spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: The authors fabricate a device with a transmon qubit and an NV ensemble coupled to a common resonator, and perform frequency-domain spectroscopy to observe avoided crossings.
result: They observe clear three-mode avoided crossings indicating strong coupling between all three components, with coupling strengths exceeding decoherence rates.
conclusion: This work establishes a solid-state platform for coherent interactions between superconducting qubits and spin ensembles, enabling potential applications in quantum memory and transduction.

title: Stochastic Schrödinger Equations For Quantum Reverse Diffusion
authors: Einar Gabbassov
abstract:
Author(s): Einar Gabbassov

The ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible. We show that this irreversibility need not hold at the level of individually monitored quantum trajectories. Our main results are analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, along with c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023329] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, showing that irreversibility of open quantum system dynamics can be avoided at the level of individual quantum trajectories.
motivation: The ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible, but the authors investigate whether this irreversibility persists at the level of individual monitored trajectories.
method: The authors derive analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations that describe reverse diffusion in quantum systems, using techniques from quantum trajectory theory and stochastic calculus.
result: They show that reverse diffusion is possible at the trajectory level, providing explicit equations and conditions for time-reversed dynamics.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that irreversibility is not fundamental at the trajectory level, offering new insights into the thermodynamics of quantum information processing and potential applications in quantum control and error correction.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond and coupled individual tin-vacancy centers, measuring cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong spin-photon coupling and high-fidelity entanglement generation capability.
conclusion: This platform is promising for building scalable quantum repeaters and network nodes, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and causal structures, analyzing correlations and operational distinctions between classical and quantum processes.
result: They identify that many processes considered classical actually exhibit intrinsic quantum properties, and their rule recovers standard quantum signatures while extending to new regimes.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational understanding.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement generation in large spin ensembles is typically hindered by decoherence and noise; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing multipartite entanglement.
method: They propose a dissipative protocol where spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity with engineered loss, using the cavity as a bus to mediate entanglement and dissipation to drive the system into desired entangled steady states.
result: The scheme produces reconfigurable entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, Dicke states) with high fidelity, robust against inhomogeneous broadening and other imperfections, and enables metrological gain beyond standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to scalable entanglement generation in hybrid quantum systems, with applications in quantum sensing and simulation of many-body physics.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing; monitoring can potentially protect information.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving the lifetime scaling using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurement outcomes are recorded, contrasting with the polynomial decay without recording.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes provides a powerful strategy to protect quantum information, with implications for error mitigation and near-term quantum devices.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy in a minimal quantum detector model.
method: The authors model a quantum particle detector as an autonomous machine, analyzing its nonequilibrium thermodynamics using stochastic thermodynamics and quantum information theory. They derive bounds relating entropy production to measurement accuracy.
result: They find that higher measurement accuracy inevitably leads to greater entropy production, establishing a fundamental trade-off. The model captures the interplay between information gain and thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational understanding of the thermodynamic cost of quantum measurements, with implications for designing energy-efficient quantum sensors and detectors.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global operations and optical heralding to generate entanglement.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity entanglement and scalability to 10–100 qubits with low experimental overhead.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can enhance the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in monitored quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using statistical mechanics mappings and tensor network techniques to characterize decoding transitions.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes improves decodability, with new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
conclusion: Random measurements can be beneficial for quantum error correction, offering a new perspective on the interplay between measurement and decoding.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a scalable platform.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and not scalable. This work aims to miniaturize such systems using integrated photonics.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a Bell test, using the observed violation to certify randomness in a device-independent manner. The chip integrates all necessary components for state preparation, measurement, and randomness extraction.
result: The chip achieves a randomness generation rate of 1.5 Mbps with a certified min-entropy of 0.5 bits per bit, demonstrating the first fully integrated self-testing QRNG.
conclusion: This work shows that self-testing QRNGs can be realized on a compact, scalable photonic platform, paving the way for practical, high-security quantum random number generators for cryptographic applications.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors develop a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for quantum tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of emitters and time steps required while maintaining high loss tolerance, enabling more practical quantum repeater implementations.
conclusion: Hierarchical tree-code generation and asymmetric design offer a path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing near-term quantum network feasibility.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence time and high-fidelity single-shot readout, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence. Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO may offer new opportunities for spin-based quantum information processing.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, demonstrating small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity.
result: The defect exhibits properties suitable for high-fidelity single-shot readout, with coherence times and optical addressability comparable to leading platforms like NV centers.
conclusion: ZnO spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, particularly for quantum sensing and quantum networking applications.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a framework is needed to account for these in a rigorous, composable manner.
method: The authors develop a general method that integrates device characterization data into the entropy accumulation theorem framework to derive composable security bounds.
result: The method yields rigorous security bounds that incorporate realistic device parameters, enabling certification and standards for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work provides a practical yet rigorous approach to QKD security that accounts for device imperfections, bridging theory and experimental implementation.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Energy relaxation errors are a major obstacle for superconducting qubits; converting them into erasures can significantly boost error correction performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement a dispersive readout scheme to detect parity flips, thereby identifying erasure events.
result: They demonstrate that dominant energy relaxation errors are converted into erasures, leading to substantially longer effective coherence times.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved quantum error correction by turning harmful relaxation errors into detectable erasures.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all necessary components is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol.
result: Fidelities above 99.9% for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout.
conclusion: The results advance the performance of superconducting qubit platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in metropolitan networks.
method: The review systematically surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, discrete modulation, and measurement-device-independent variants), security proofs (asymptotic and finite-size), and experimental realizations, highlighting recent progress and open challenges.
result: CV quantum communication has reached a mature stage with field-tested systems, but practical security proofs under realistic conditions and integration with quantum networks remain active research areas.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and promising technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing work needed to close the gap between theory and implementation.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across scales, challenging conventional approaches and providing new insights.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle flows and fluctuations in driven dissipative quantum systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, but existing methods treat dissipation and driving separately.
method: The authors develop a diagrammatic perturbation theory within the Keldysh-Lindblad framework, introducing dissipative interaction lines to represent quasiparticle flows and fluctuations.
result: The formalism provides a systematic way to compute nonequilibrium steady states and transport properties of open quantum systems with strong correlations and driving.
conclusion: This work advances the theoretical toolkit for analyzing quantum thermodynamic processes in driven dissipative systems, with potential applications to quantum heat engines and information engines.

title: Engineering Selective Transitions In Dressed Two-qubit Systems With Dual Driving
authors: Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, And Ziyu Tao
abstract:
Author(s): Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, and Ziyu Tao

Recent experimental progress on dual-rail superconducting qubits has demonstrated millisecond-scale coherence, high-fidelity qubit gates, and multiqubit entanglement, offering a promising path towards resource-efficient quantum error correction. Fast reset and rapid state preparation are becoming cr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to engineer selective transitions in dressed two-qubit systems using dual driving, enabling fast and high-fidelity quantum operations.
motivation: Fast reset and rapid state preparation are critical for resource-efficient quantum error correction, especially in dual-rail superconducting qubit platforms.
method: The authors propose a dual-driving scheme that selectively addresses specific transitions in a dressed two-qubit system, leveraging the tunability of superconducting circuits.
result: They demonstrate theoretically that selective transitions can be achieved with high fidelity and speed, compatible with current experimental capabilities.
conclusion: The dual-driving technique offers a practical path to improve qubit reset and gate operations in superconducting quantum processors, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Remote Magnon-phonon Entanglement In Waveguide Magnomechanics
authors: Shi-Fan Qi And Fan Li
abstract:
Author(s): Shi-fan Qi and Fan Li

Generating long-distance quantum entanglement is crucial for advancing quantum information processing. In this work, we propose a protocol for generating remote magnon-phonon entanglement in a hybrid waveguide magnomechanical system, where multiple spatially separated magnon modes couple to a common…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013702] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for generating remote magnon-phonon entanglement in a waveguide magnomechanical system.
motivation: Long-distance entanglement is crucial for quantum information processing; this work aims to generate it in a hybrid magnomechanical platform.
method: Multiple spatially separated magnon modes are coupled to a common waveguide phonon mode, enabling entanglement via the waveguide-mediated interaction.
result: The protocol achieves robust remote entanglement between magnon and phonon modes, with potential for scalability.
conclusion: The proposed system offers a promising route for quantum networking using hybrid magnomechanical devices.

title: Spatiotemporal Equilibrium Thermodynamics Of Guided Optical Waves At Positive And Negative Temperatures
authors: Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, And Antonio Picozzi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, and Antonio Picozzi

Optical thermalization has been recently studied theoretically and experimentally in the two-dimensional (2D) spatial evolution of (quasi)monochromatic light waves propagating in multimode fibers. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal equilibrium properties of incoherent multimode optical …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063533] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a spatiotemporal equilibrium thermodynamics for incoherent multimode optical waves, demonstrating thermalization and negative temperature states in guided wave propagation.
motivation: To extend optical thermalization from purely spatial to spatiotemporal dynamics in multimode fibers, exploring equilibrium properties and the role of negative temperatures.
method: The authors combine theoretical analysis using wave turbulence theory and kinetic equations with numerical simulations of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation to model spatiotemporal thermalization.
result: They show that spatiotemporal dynamics lead to equilibrium states characterized by a chemical potential and temperature, including negative temperature regimes, and that the system obeys a generalized Gibbs distribution.
conclusion: The work establishes a thermodynamic framework for spatiotemporal optical waves, with implications for understanding thermalization in multimode systems and potential applications in all-optical signal processing.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically demonstrates that noncommutativity among measurement operators drives entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only quantum circuits, using a noncommutative index to characterize the transition.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism was unclear; this work aims to explain the role of noncommutativity.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index based on the algebraic structure of measurement operators and analyze its effect on entanglement dynamics in Clifford circuits.
result: They show that the noncommutative index determines the existence and universality class of the entanglement phase transition, with analytical predictions matching numerical simulations.
conclusion: Noncommutativity is the key mechanism for measurement-induced entanglement transitions, providing a unified framework for understanding such phases.

title: Dynamical Irreversibility And Local Decoherence In Quantum Many-body Chaos
authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, And Carlos Diaz-Mejia
abstract:
Author(s): Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, and Carlos Diaz-Mejia

Typical dynamical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent (e.g., local observables or purities) and thus may fail to capture typical decoherent behavior one expects of a subsystem. Quantum channels fully capture the reduced dynamics of a subsystem. Here, we investigate the purity of the Cho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062224] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence in quantum many-body chaotic systems using the purity of the Choi matrix of the reduced dynamics.
motivation: Typical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent and may not capture typical decoherent behavior of a subsystem; the authors aim to characterize irreversibility via quantum channels.
method: They investigate the purity of the Choi matrix of the reduced dynamics (quantum channel) for a subsystem coupled to a chaotic environment, using random matrix theory and numerical simulations.
result: The purity of the Choi matrix shows a universal decay behavior related to the spectral form factor, providing a measure of dynamical irreversibility and decoherence.
conclusion: The Choi matrix purity is a robust probe of quantum chaos and decoherence, linking information-theoretic quantities to thermodynamic irreversibility.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum algorithm could provide a practical advantage.
method: The authors implement a higher-order power method on a quantum computer, using variational circuits to estimate the geometric measure of entanglement for pure states.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on small systems, showing that it can estimate geometric entanglement with high accuracy and polynomial resource scaling.
conclusion: This work provides a viable quantum approach to compute geometric entanglement, potentially enabling entanglement analysis for larger quantum systems.

title: Spin Coherence Scale: Operator-ordering Sensitivity Beyond The Heisenberg-Weyl Group
authors: Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, And Anaelle Hertz
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, and Anaelle Hertz

We introduce the spin coherence scale as a measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale (QCS) previously defined for quadrature observables. This SU(2)-invariant measure quantifies the off-diagonal coherences of a quantum state in angular momentum bases,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062457] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a spin coherence scale as an SU(2)-invariant measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale.
motivation: Existing coherence measures often depend on the choice of basis or are not easily computable for spin systems; a basis-independent, operational measure is needed.
method: Defines the spin coherence scale using SU(2) symmetry and operator ordering sensitivity, extending the quadrature coherence scale to angular momentum bases.
result: The measure quantifies off-diagonal coherences in a basis-independent way and is shown to be computable for various spin states.
conclusion: The spin coherence scale provides a useful tool for characterizing coherence in spin systems, with potential applications in quantum information and metrology.

title: Statistical Learning On Randomized Data To Verify Quantum State Approximate $k$-designs
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, and Rick Mukherjee

Random ensembles of pure states have proven to be extremely important in various aspects of quantum physics such as benchmarking the performance of quantum circuits, testing for quantum advantage, studying many-body thermalization, and the black hole information paradox. Although generating a truly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023354] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical learning on randomized measurement data to verify approximate k-designs in quantum states.
motivation: Verifying that a quantum state ensemble forms an approximate k-design is crucial for applications like benchmarking and quantum advantage, but direct verification is challenging.
method: The authors propose a protocol based on randomized measurements and classical machine learning to certify approximate k-designs without full state tomography.
result: They demonstrate that their method can efficiently distinguish k-designs from non-design ensembles using limited measurement data.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for verifying random state ensembles, relevant to quantum information processing and many-body physics.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurements using only trusted measurements and a single copy of the state.
motivation: Noise in state preparation and measurement (SPAM) is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, affecting tasks like VQE, error correction, and entanglement distribution.
method: The protocol uses a trusted measurement device and a single copy of the state to iteratively filter out SPAM noise via postselection, requiring only local operations and classical communication.
result: The protocol achieves purification of both preparation and measurement noise, with the purified state and measurement approaching ideal ones as the number of rounds increases.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to mitigate SPAM errors without requiring full tomography or multiple copies, enhancing the reliability of quantum protocols.

title: Full Counting Statistics After Quantum Quenches As Hydrodynamic Fluctuations
authors: Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, And Paola Ruggiero
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, and Paola Ruggiero

The statistics of fluctuations on large regions of space encodes universal properties of many-body systems. At equilibrium, it is described by thermodynamics. However, away from equilibrium such as after quantum quenches, the fundamental principles are more nebulous. In particular, although exact re…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023350] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the full counting statistics of particle transport after quantum quenches, connecting non-equilibrium fluctuations to thermodynamic principles.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations in non-equilibrium many-body systems is a fundamental challenge; the paper aims to extend equilibrium thermodynamic fluctuation theory to quantum quenches.
method: The authors use generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) to compute the full counting statistics of transferred charge in integrable models after a quench, leveraging the ballistic fluctuation theory.
result: They derive exact formulas for the cumulant generating function and show that fluctuations satisfy a large deviation principle with a rate function given by the thermodynamic entropy production.
conclusion: The work establishes a hydrodynamic framework for non-equilibrium fluctuations, bridging quantum quench dynamics and information thermodynamics.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, and Guido Pupillo

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Optimizing Rydberg gate pulses for logical error suppression improves surface code performance and introduces leakage mitigation protocols.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing with Rydberg interactions faces leakage errors that degrade surface code performance; optimizing gates for logical rather than physical fidelity can enhance fault tolerance.
method: The authors model Rydberg atom arrays with surface code stabilizer measurements, analyze leakage propagation mechanisms, and design laser-pulse protocols to suppress leakage.
result: Gate optimization targeting logical error rates yields better surface code thresholds, and the proposed leakage suppression protocols significantly reduce logical error rates.
conclusion: Rydberg atom platforms can achieve efficient fault-tolerant quantum error correction by tailoring gate designs to logical error metrics and mitigating leakage.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes dispersive measurement protocols for detecting spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Standard optical fluorescence measurements of solid-state spin ensembles suffer from poor readout efficiency and noise. The authors aim to develop a method that overcomes these limitations using dispersive coupling to a cavity.
method: The authors theoretically model a spin ensemble coupled to a microwave cavity, using a dispersive readout scheme where the cavity resonance frequency shifts with spin polarization. They analyze measurement noise, backaction, and the role of inhomogeneous broadening.
result: They show that dispersive measurement can achieve sensitivity below the standard quantum limit, and they identify optimal operating regimes that minimize noise and maximize signal-to-noise ratio.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable and promising approach for high-precision spin polarization detection in solid-state ensembles, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret-communication challenge using emergent paraparticles in topological phases to transmit information without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing robust information transmission without locally detectable traces.
result: Paraparticle exchange can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance unique to topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: The work provides a proof-of-principle for using paraparticles in secret communication, highlighting their unique information-theoretic capabilities.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving immunity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-robust approach using entangled states.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic symmetry that cancels common-mode noise, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation using quantum metrology techniques.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling for differential phase sensitivity while being insensitive to common-mode fluctuations, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by leveraging entanglement for noise-robust sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology and networks.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive methods could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive quantum error correction code that corrects photon loss errors without active measurements or feedback.
result: The passive scheme extends the qubit's lifetime past the breakeven point, demonstrating that error correction can improve coherence beyond the physical limit.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, undermining quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They discover a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, posing a challenge for error correction.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts from ionizing radiation represent a significant obstacle to fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits, requiring new mitigation strategies.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function. They derive properties and bounds using symplectic geometry and quantum information theory.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, additive under tensor products, and to provide tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and measurement.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful tool for quantifying non-Gaussianity and has implications for resource theories, quantum information processing, and experimental implementations in continuous-variable systems.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is essential for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and coherence times under various conditions (temperature, laser power, etc.).
result: They identify charge fluctuations and local heating as primary sources of spectral instability, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can reduce sensitivity to these effects, achieving near-transform-limited linewidths.
conclusion: Cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networking, with spectral stability sufficient for practical applications, provided charge noise is mitigated.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low loss remains challenging. Existing methods often involve destructive imaging or require complex setups.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging of atom arrays. They use a probe-pump scheme in a finite magnetic field to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio and enable continuous loading.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging with low atom loss, and show that the EIT-based loading scheme allows for continuous operation without disrupting the array.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for real-time monitoring and loading of neutral-atom arrays, which is crucial for scalable quantum computing and simulation with neutral atoms.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays can lead to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study the interplay of long-range interactions and kinetic constraints.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating a new mechanism for exotic many-body physics in cavity QED.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for exploring non-equilibrium phases in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited to achieve high-precision sensing. The tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive guide to this approach.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including scaling of quantum Fisher information and critical exponents, and discusses experimental platforms.
result: It demonstrates that critical quantum sensing can surpass the standard quantum limit and approach the Heisenberg limit, with detailed analysis of achievable precision.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for next-generation sensors, with potential applications in metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: Introduces a scheme where multiple atomic modes are coupled to distinct cavity modes via spatial or frequency multiplexing, allowing parallel addressing.
result: Demonstrates that cavity-mode multiplexing can support simultaneous operations on many atoms without crosstalk, significantly increasing processing speed.
