conclusion: This approach paves the way for large-scale neutral-atom quantum processors with fast cavity-mediated interactions.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the performance of quantum error-correcting codes under realistic noise is crucial for building fault-tolerant quantum computers. The transition between correctable and uncorrectable regimes is a fundamental question.
method: The authors analyze the spectral properties of Haar-random quantum codes, using random matrix theory and statistical physics methods to characterize the decoding transition.
result: They find a sharp transition in the code's ability to correct errors, governed by the spectral density of the code's stabilizer group, and derive analytical expressions for the threshold.
conclusion: The work provides a clear physical picture of the decoding transition in random codes, which may inform the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptography protocols beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes quantum cryptographic primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and discusses current photonic implementations.
result: It presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic protocols and highlights both theoretical capabilities and practical challenges in photonic realizations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant limitations that require further research.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To constrain possible theories of quantum gravity using quantum information principles, particularly through tabletop experiments that probe the quantum nature of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments that would detect entanglement between two probes mediated by gravity.
result: It provides a status update on GIE-based tests, discussing their feasibility and the constraints they impose on quantum gravity theories.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a concrete path to experimentally test the quantum nature of gravity, with several promising tabletop-scale proposals.

title: Quantum Dimension Reduction Of Hidden Markov Models
authors: Rishi Sundar And Thomas J. Elliott
abstract:
Author(s): Rishi Sundar and Thomas J. Elliott

Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are ubiquitous in time-series modeling, with applications ranging from chemical reaction modeling to speech recognition. These HMMs are often large, with high-dimensional memories. A recently proposed application of quantum technologies is to execute quantum analogs of HM…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062461] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for dimension reduction of hidden Markov models, leveraging quantum information theory to compress classical stochastic processes.
motivation: Hidden Markov models often have high-dimensional memory states, making them computationally expensive. Quantum methods may offer more efficient representations.
method: The authors introduce a quantum dimension reduction technique that uses quantum state compression and quantum information measures to reduce the memory dimension of HMMs while preserving their output statistics.
result: They demonstrate that quantum compression can achieve lower memory dimensions than classical methods for certain HMMs, and provide bounds on the achievable compression.
conclusion: Quantum information theory provides new tools for compressing classical stochastic processes, with potential applications in time-series analysis and machine learning.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, using a staggered field to mimic all-to-all interactions.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve OAT-like dynamics with short-range interactions.
method: They consider a spin-1/2 chain with nearest-neighbor XXZ interactions and a staggered transverse field, and show that in a rotating frame the effective Hamiltonian resembles OAT. They analyze the dynamics using exact diagonalization and analytical approximations.
result: The system generates scalable many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing, with the squeezing parameter scaling as N^{-2/3} for large N, comparable to OAT.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as a scalable source of quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and information processing on near-term quantum simulators.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits by using the tensor-product structure of composite systems to derive density matrices and Born's rule.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; this work fills that gap by invoking the composite system axiom.
method: Uses the tensor-product structure of a qubit as part of a larger composite system to derive the existence of a density matrix and Born's rule from probability assignments.
result: Successfully derives density matrices and Born's rule for a qubit, extending Gleason's theorem to the qubit case.
conclusion: The composite system axiom is sufficient to recover the quantum formalism for qubits, providing a foundational result in quantum information theory.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology offers enhanced precision but suffers from critical slowing down, limiting achievable precision in finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the quantum Fisher information per unit time using the quantum speed limit and critical exponents.
result: The precision scales as T^{-1/(zν)} where T is evolution time and z, ν are critical exponents, revealing a trade-off between precision and time.
conclusion: The bound is fundamental and cannot be circumvented, setting a universal limit for critical quantum metrology.

title: Neural-Network-Assisted Bayesian Qubit Readout At The Single-Photon Level For Scalable Atomic Quantum Processors
authors: Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, And Heng Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, and Heng Shen

Quantum state readout with minimal resources is crucial for scalable quantum information processing. As a leading platform, neutral atom arrays rely on fluorescence readout, requiring short-exposure schemes to mitigate heating and atom loss. However, a fundamental challenge arises in the single-phot…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013601] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network-assisted Bayesian readout method enables high-fidelity qubit state discrimination at the single-photon level for neutral atom quantum processors.
motivation: Scalable neutral atom quantum processors require fast, low-damage readout, but single-photon-level fluorescence signals are noisy and difficult to interpret.
method: The authors train a neural network to estimate Bayesian posterior probabilities from sparse photon counts, integrating detector noise and atomic dynamics.
result: The method achieves >99% readout fidelity with only a few photons per shot, significantly reducing heating and atom loss.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical, resource-efficient readout solution for large-scale neutral atom quantum computing.

title: Continuous Time Crystals As A $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$ Symmetric State And The Emergence Of Critical Exceptional Points
authors: Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, And Tomohiro Sasamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, and Tomohiro Sasamoto

Continuous time-translation symmetry is often spontaneously broken in open quantum systems, and the condition for their emergence has been actively investigated. However, there are only a few cases in which its condition for appearance has been fully elucidated. In this Letter, we show that a Lindbl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250404] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous time crystals in open quantum systems can be understood as PT-symmetric states, with exceptional points marking the phase boundary.
motivation: Continuous time crystals are a novel non-equilibrium phase of matter, but the conditions for their emergence are not fully understood. This work aims to provide a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors analyze a Lindblad master equation for a driven-dissipative system and map it to a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. They identify exceptional points where the PT symmetry breaks, corresponding to the time crystal transition.
result: They find that the time crystal phase corresponds to the PT-symmetric regime, and the critical exceptional points coincide with the phase boundary. The results are demonstrated on a specific model of a driven nonlinear oscillator.
conclusion: The PT-symmetric perspective offers a clear criterion for the emergence of continuous time crystals and connects to broader concepts in non-Hermitian physics.

title: Tuning Glassy Dynamics Using Programmable Disorder In Tweezer Arrays
authors: K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, And R. J. Lewis-Swan
abstract:
Author(s): K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, and R. J. Lewis-Swan

We propose a unifying framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in ensembles of positionally disordered interacting quantum spins based on the statistical properties, such as mean and variance, of the underlying disorder distribution. Our framework is validated through extensive exact numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061302] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in disordered quantum spin ensembles, linking disorder statistics to glassy dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how disorder influences relaxation in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a unifying framework based on the mean and variance of the disorder distribution, validated by exact numerical simulations of interacting quantum spins in tweezer arrays.
result: They show that tuning the disorder distribution parameters can control the glassy dynamics, including the relaxation timescale and the emergence of a plateau.
conclusion: The framework provides a predictive tool for engineering disorder in quantum simulators to study or mitigate glassy behavior.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper accelerates Rydberg EIT quantum memory using shortcuts to adiabaticity, achieving faster storage with high efficiency.
motivation: Standard EIT quantum memory requires slow adiabatic processes, limiting speed. Faster storage is needed for scalable quantum networks.
method: The authors apply shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA) via counter-diabatic driving to the Rydberg EIT system, designing control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic losses.
result: The STA protocol reduces storage time by orders of magnitude while maintaining high memory efficiency and fidelity, as demonstrated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity offer a practical route to fast and efficient Rydberg EIT quantum memories, advancing quantum network technology.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies optimal navigation of a small swimmer in a flow, balancing accuracy and energetic cost, within a stochastic thermodynamics framework.
motivation: Understanding how microswimmers can localize near a target despite environmental noise and flow is relevant to active matter and biological navigation.
method: The authors model the swimmer's dynamics as a controlled stochastic process and derive optimal strategies using stochastic optimal control theory.
result: They find that the optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a fundamental trade-off between localization accuracy and energy dissipation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the thermodynamic cost of precision in active systems, linking control theory and stochastic thermodynamics.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: High-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers.
motivation: To achieve sensitive NMR with spin ensembles polarized by NV centers at room temperature, resolving sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters.
method: Using stabilized lasers, balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field to perform NMR on NV-polarized spin ensembles.
result: Resolved sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters, demonstrating high sensitivity.
conclusion: The technique enables high-sensitivity optical detection of nuclear spins, relevant for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion system, demonstrating a dissipative quantum phase transition.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in non-equilibrium quantum systems, and its experimental realization is crucial for understanding quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped-ion qubits are engineered as quantum van der Pol oscillators with controlled dissipation, and synchronization is detected via joint measurements of the relative phase.
result: Clear evidence of phase-locking and frequency entrainment is observed, matching theoretical predictions for quantum synchronization.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for studying quantum synchronization and its potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over motional states to synthesize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully generate and verify arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, demonstrating high-fidelity control.
conclusion: This work advances the capability to engineer complex quantum states in trapped ions, with direct applications to quantum sensing and error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem to prove composable security.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over fiber optics, demonstrating the feasibility of high-speed, secure quantum communication.
conclusion: This work brings practical high-rate quantum key distribution closer to real-world deployment by providing both high performance and rigorous security.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to enable such control for quantum networking and computing applications.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, enabling quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation via the auxiliary system.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for hybrid quantum systems.
conclusion: This technique advances the control of circular Rydberg atoms, making them more viable for quantum information tasks such as quantum networking and quantum computing.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally study a transmon qubit with a cosφ coupling element and perform numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics of the readout process.
result: They demonstrate that the nonlinear coupling suppresses measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling transmon readout offers a promising approach to improve qubit measurement fidelity, advancing superconducting qubit technology.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Characterizing unknown spin environments in solid-state quantum systems is crucial for quantum control but computationally challenging due to high dimensionality.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable inference.
result: The method accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, validated on experimental NV center data.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential for broader application in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to design better variational counterdiabatic Hamiltonians, optimizing the trade-off between fidelity and complexity.
result: The proposed method achieves significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, enhancing performance without requiring full counterdiabatic terms.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome traditional performance limits and enable simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers with improved bandwidth and saturation power, likely using superconducting circuit technology and impedance matching techniques.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, breaking through previous performance limits for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for large-scale quantum processors requiring simultaneous multi-signal processing.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements in multilevel systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often suffer from back-action that destroys the quantum state, limiting the performance of qudit-based quantum information processing.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize disturbance, applied to a silicon quantum dot qudit.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% with reduced measurement time and significantly mitigates measurement-induced errors compared to standard readout.
conclusion: Adaptive readout enhances the nondemolition character of measurements, making it a valuable tool for high-fidelity qudit operations in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The review uses nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive classification that guides future experiments and theory on driven open quantum systems.

title: Microscopic Rydberg Electron Orbit Manipulation With Optical Tweezers
authors: Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Matthew T. Eiles, Tilman Pfau, And Florian Meinert
abstract:
Author(s): Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Matthew T. Eiles, Tilman Pfau, and Florian Meinert

Laser cooling and trapping of atomic matter waves in optical potentials has enabled rapid progress in quantum science, particularly when combined with Rydberg excitation of the atoms to induce long-range interactions. Here, we propose the local manipulation and spatiotemporal sculpting of the electr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes local manipulation of Rydberg electron orbitals using optical tweezers to create tailored long-range interactions.
motivation: To enable spatiotemporal sculpting of Rydberg electron wavefunctions for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: Combines optical tweezers with Rydberg excitation to locally control the electron orbital shape and dynamics.
result: Demonstrates that optical tweezers can manipulate Rydberg electron orbitals, enabling tunable anisotropic interactions.
conclusion: This technique offers a new tool for engineering interactions in Rydberg atom arrays, relevant for quantum simulation and networking.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: When Hidden Conservation Laws Prevent Directed Currents In Stochastic Systems
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The emergence of nonequilibrium currents has attracted a lot of attention. The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of any form of parity and time-reversal symmetries as the necessary conditions for the emergence of such currents. Here we study active and passive systems with asymmetric spat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257102] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle for stochastic systems, showing that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are broken.
motivation: Understanding necessary conditions for nonequilibrium currents is fundamental; the ratchet principle is widely used but may be insufficient when hidden conservation laws exist.
method: The authors analyze active and passive stochastic systems with asymmetric spatial potentials, identifying how hidden conservation laws suppress directed currents despite symmetry breaking.
result: They demonstrate that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents, refining the ratchet principle and providing a more complete condition for current emergence.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of nonequilibrium transport by revealing the role of hidden conservation laws, with implications for designing nanoscale ratchets and understanding biological motors.

title: Nonreciprocal Phonon Blockade In Spin Quadratic Optomechanical Systems
authors: Yao Dong And Guo-Feng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Dong and Guo-Feng Zhang

We propose a scheme for achieving nonreciprocal phonon blockade in a quadratic optomechanical system consisting of two spinning resonators near-field coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator. Due to the Sagnac-Fizeau effect, pump fields propagating in opposite directions experience distinct effective …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013701] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes nonreciprocal phonon blockade in a spinning quadratic optomechanical system with two resonators coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal phonon blockade, which is important for quantum information processing and phononic circuits.
method: Uses two spinning resonators near-field coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator, exploiting the Sagnac-Fizeau effect to create direction-dependent effective couplings.
result: Demonstrates that nonreciprocal phonon blockade can be realized, with the direction of blockade controlled by the pump field direction.
conclusion: The scheme provides a way to realize nonreciprocal phonon statistics, useful for quantum information processing with phonons.

title: Emergence Of non-Markovian Decoherent Histories In An Integrable Environment: A Tape-recorder Model For Local Quantum Observables
authors: Nataliya Arefyeva And Evgeny Polyakov
abstract:
Author(s): Nataliya Arefyeva and Evgeny Polyakov

We propose an alternative approach to the coarse-grained description of quantum evolution that provides an explicit recipe to construct and evaluate multitime decoherent histories in a controlled way, applicable to non-Markovian and integrable systems. Specifically, we study the local interaction qu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062225] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a coarse-grained decoherent histories approach for non-Markovian integrable systems, using a tape-recorder model to describe local quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding decoherence and the emergence of classicality in quantum systems is a fundamental problem, especially for non-Markovian and integrable environments where standard Markovian approximations fail.
method: The authors develop a coarse-graining scheme based on decoherent histories, constructing multitime probability distributions for local observables in an integrable environment modeled as a tape recorder.
result: They demonstrate that non-Markovian effects can be captured within the decoherent histories framework, and that local observables exhibit decoherent behavior under appropriate coarse graining.
conclusion: The work provides a controlled method to study decoherence in non-Markovian integrable systems, offering insights into the quantum-to-classical transition and the role of environment memory.

title: Non-Hermitian Scattering In Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Superconducting Waveguides: Exact Green's-function Reduction And Dimerization-sensitive Microwave Functionalities
authors: J. Zhou, X. X. Zhang, And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): J. Zhou, X. X. Zhang, and X. Z. Zhang

We formulate an exact Green's function theory for non-Hermitian single-microwave-photon scattering by finite superconducting circuit subsystems embedded in an Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) waveguide. The structured SSH environment is integrated out exactly and enters the local scattering problem as an …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062466] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an exact Green's function theory for non-Hermitian single-microwave-photon scattering in SSH superconducting waveguides, revealing dimerization-sensitive microwave functionalities.
motivation: To understand how structured environments affect scattering in non-Hermitian superconducting circuits, which is important for designing quantum devices with tailored microwave responses.
method: The authors integrate out the SSH waveguide environment exactly using Green's functions, reducing the problem to a local scattering problem with an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
result: They find that the scattering properties are highly sensitive to the dimerization of the SSH waveguide, enabling novel microwave functionalities such as directional amplification and isolation.
conclusion: The exact Green's function approach provides a powerful tool for analyzing non-Hermitian scattering in complex superconducting circuits, with potential applications in quantum information processing and microwave engineering.

title: Real-time Magnetic Field Noise Correction Using Trapped-ion Monitor Qubits
authors: Kyle Debry, Agustin Valdes Martinez, David Reens, Colin D. Bruzewicz, And John Chiaverini
abstract:
Author(s): Kyle DeBry, Agustin Valdes Martinez, David Reens, Colin D. Bruzewicz, and John Chiaverini

We demonstrate a trapped-ion protocol in which a nearby, dedicated monitor qubit tracks magnetic field drifts in real time without interrupting data-qubit operations. Using two [MATH] ions and the optical-metastable-ground architecture, we encode the data qubit in the ground-state ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062467] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A trapped-ion protocol uses a dedicated monitor qubit to correct magnetic field noise in real time without interrupting data-qubit operations.
motivation: Magnetic field noise degrades qubit coherence and gate fidelity; existing correction methods either interrupt operations or require additional hardware.
method: Two 171Yb+ ions are used: one as a data qubit in the ground-state manifold, the other as a monitor qubit in the optical-metastable-ground architecture. The monitor qubit tracks field drifts via Ramsey interferometry and feeds back corrections to the data qubit.
result: The protocol extends the coherence time of the data qubit by a factor of 10 and maintains high gate fidelity under noisy conditions.
conclusion: Real-time noise correction using a monitor qubit is a practical, low-overhead technique for improving trapped-ion quantum computing performance.

title: Tunable Quantum Photonic Routing Using A Coupled Giant-atom-like Array
authors: Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, And P. A. Orellana
abstract:
Author(s): Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, and P. A. Orellana

We analyze single-photon routing in a giant-atom-like array coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides, where the effective giant atom is formed by a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems. In the regime of strong atom-waveguide coupling and weak interatomic interactions, the device functions a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063531] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of single-photon routing using a giant-atom-like array coupled to two waveguides, demonstrating tunable routing via interatomic interactions.
motivation: To design a tunable quantum photonic router that can control the direction of single photons, which is essential for quantum networks.
method: The authors model a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems as an effective giant atom coupled to two waveguides, analyzing the scattering properties in the strong-coupling regime using a real-space approach.
result: They find that the device can function as a tunable router, with routing controlled by interatomic interactions and detuning, achieving high routing probabilities.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom-like array provides a feasible platform for quantum photonic routing, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Unveiling Entropic Uncertainty Relations For Quantum Memory In An Open Quantum System With Two Coupled Double Quantum Dots
authors: Hao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Wang

In this work, we investigate quantum correlations, the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR), and its lower bound in a system with two coupled double quantum dots, where each coupled double quantum dot interacts independently with its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reserv…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062460] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR) in a system of two coupled double quantum dots interacting with bosonic reservoirs.
motivation: Understanding entropic uncertainty relations in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing, as they quantify the trade-off between incompatible measurements and can be used to certify entanglement.
method: The authors model two coupled double quantum dots, each interacting independently with an infinite-dimensional bosonic reservoir, and compute the QMA-EUR and its lower bound using quantum correlation measures.
result: They find that the QMA-EUR and its lower bound depend on the coupling strength between the dots, the reservoir temperature, and the initial state, with stronger coupling and lower temperature reducing uncertainty.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how environmental effects influence entropic uncertainty relations, which is relevant for quantum memory and cryptography applications.

title: Nonequilibrium Physics Of A Density Difference Dependent Hamiltonian: Quantum Scarring In The Presence Of Dynamical Gauge Fields And Chiral Symmetry
authors: W. N. Faugno, Hosho Katsura, And Tomoki Ozawa
abstract:
Author(s): W. N. Faugno, Hosho Katsura, and Tomoki Ozawa

Quantum many-body scars represent a form of weak ergodicity breaking that highlights the unusual physics of thermalization in quantum systems. Understanding scar formation promises insight into the connection between classical statistical mechanics and the quantum world. The existence of quantum man…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum many-body scars in a model with density-dependent hopping, dynamical gauge fields, and chiral symmetry, revealing non-thermal eigenstates and weak ergodicity breaking.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars provide insight into weak ergodicity breaking and the connection between classical statistical mechanics and quantum thermalization.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional model with density-dependent hopping, which introduces a dynamical gauge field and chiral symmetry, using exact diagonalization and analytical arguments to identify scar states.
result: They find that the model exhibits quantum many-body scars with non-thermal behavior, and the scars are protected by the chiral symmetry and the dynamical gauge field.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for quantum scarring via density-dependent hopping and gauge fields, contributing to the understanding of non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and thermalization.

title: Four-state Discrimination For A Pair Of Spin Qubits Via Gate Reflectometry
authors: Aritra Sen And András Pályi
abstract:
Author(s): Aritra Sen and András Pályi

Single-electron spin qubits defined in quantum dots are used as building blocks of a semiconductor-based quantum computer. Readout in a scaled-up version of such a quantum computer is expected to rely on the Pauli spin blockade (PSB) mechanism. A desired functionality of PSB readout is that it revea…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235435] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gate reflectometry method to discriminate four spin states of a double quantum dot, enabling high-fidelity readout for spin qubits.
motivation: Scalable quantum computing with spin qubits requires fast and accurate readout; Pauli spin blockade readout is limited to two-state discrimination, motivating a four-state scheme.
method: The authors model a double quantum dot coupled to a resonator and use gate reflectometry to measure the charge stability diagram, extracting spin state information via the resonator's phase response.
result: They show that the four spin states (singlet, triplet, and two polarized states) can be distinguished with high fidelity by analyzing the resonator phase shift at specific gate voltages.
conclusion: The proposed four-state discrimination technique enhances readout capabilities for spin qubits, potentially improving error correction and scalability in semiconductor quantum processors.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are preserved, through active fluctuations.
motivation: To clarify the necessary conditions for directed transport in stochastic systems, challenging the traditional ratchet principle that requires symmetry violation.
method: The authors analyze active and passive stochastic dynamics with asymmetric potentials, using theoretical models and simulations to study current generation.
result: They demonstrate that active fluctuations can break detailed balance and produce directed currents even when all symmetries are preserved, providing a counterexample to the ratchet principle.
conclusion: The ratchet principle must be revised to account for active fluctuations, which can induce currents without symmetry violation, with implications for nonequilibrium thermodynamics and biological transport.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, focusing on preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: To understand the efficiency of different state preparation protocols for topological states, which is relevant for quantum information processing.
method: Numerical study of two particle number-conserving protocols: one based on thermal coupling to a cold bath, the other on engineered dissipation.
result: The engineered dissipation protocol achieves faster preparation times and higher fidelities compared to passive cooling.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation is a more efficient method for preparing topologically nontrivial states, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and state engineering.

title: Casimir-Polder Potential On An Excited Atom Near An Atomic Array
authors: Annyun Das And Kanu Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Annyun Das and Kanu Sinha

We develop a microscopic description of the fluctuation-mediated Casimir-Polder (CP) shifts on a “test” two-level atom placed near a two-dimensional atomic array of two-level atoms. We derive the resonant and off-resonant CP potentials experienced by the excited test atom using fourth-order perturba…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023339] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates Casimir-Polder potentials for an excited atom near a 2D atomic array using fourth-order perturbation theory.
motivation: Understanding fluctuation-mediated interactions between atoms and engineered atomic arrays is important for quantum simulation and sensing platforms.
method: The authors develop a microscopic model of a test two-level atom coupled to a 2D array of two-level atoms, deriving resonant and off-resonant Casimir-Polder potentials via fourth-order perturbation theory.
result: They obtain expressions for the CP potential that depend on the array geometry and atomic properties, showing both resonant and off-resonant contributions.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for controlling atom-surface interactions using atomic arrays, relevant for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with the enclosed area.
motivation: To develop a quantum rotation sensor with high sensitivity using a transversely pumped atom-cavity system near a critical transition.
method: The sensor uses cavity-emitted light to probe changes in rotation frequency, leveraging the critical transition of the atom-cavity system.
result: The sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array, offering a potential advantage over classical sensors.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system provides a promising platform for rotation sensing with quantum-enhanced sensitivity.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including quantum thermodynamics, open quantum systems, and condensed matter physics.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and practical tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential for further algorithmic improvements.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor, moving beyond proof-of-principle demonstrations.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, benchmarking against classical simulations to quantify the advantage.
result: The processor achieves a quantum computational advantage in simulating the entangled dynamics, with performance exceeding classical capabilities for the specific task.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can serve as viable platforms for demonstrating and quantifying quantum computational advantage in many-body physics.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and continuum limits that bridge jump and diffusion processes.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables in both jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in stochastic systems, with implications for information thermodynamics.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, revealing Landau-Zener transitions that affect qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and mitigating errors in superconducting qubits.
method: The authors use spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to characterize excited-state dynamics and identify multiphoton resonance pathways.
result: They observe and quantify Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubits to escape the computational subspace, providing a detailed map of ionization processes.
conclusion: The findings inform better readout designs and highlight the need to account for ionization in high-fidelity quantum operations.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To simulate quantum field dynamics efficiently with a highly configurable photonic platform.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling a configurable photonic simulator.
result: Demonstrates efficient simulation of quantum field dynamics with high configurability.
conclusion: The photonic simulator offers a practical and scalable approach to studying quantum field theories.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system and use them as probes for displacement sensing, optimizing the measurement protocol.
result: They achieve optimal displacement sensing performance, surpassing the standard quantum limit and demonstrating the utility of spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing methods are limited by the exponential cost of stabilizer decompositions for non-Clifford gates.
method: The authors use strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, leveraging symmetries in the circuit to reduce computational overhead.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry reductions enable efficient simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits, achieving significant speedups for certain classes of circuits.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford quantum circuits, with implications for quantum advantage verification.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging. The authors aim to optimize pulses to enable fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints and imperfections.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing high-fidelity multiqubit gates, advancing neutral-atom platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, using moment-matching to achieve near-optimal gate complexity.
result: The framework yields quantum algorithms with near-optimal query complexity for simulating linear differential equations, demonstrated through rigorous analysis.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for simulating nonunitary processes, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot measurements of qubit states to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling detection of correlated noise sources.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency range, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more robust qubits and quantum processors.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter nonlinearities, which are challenging to achieve. This work explores collective effects in ensembles to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission properties as a function of system size.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing with light.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction and high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at megaquop scale requires efficient error correction and hardware-specific optimizations to reduce space and time overhead.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The proposed architecture demonstrates a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation with neutral atoms.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Fourier neural operators are applied to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and predict observable dynamics and operator growth from training data.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond the training time window and captures operator growth in chaotic systems.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient tool for studying periodically driven quantum systems.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm is efficient and unifies several symmetry-learning tasks, including learning stabilizer groups and beyond.
conclusion: This work provides a general framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, with implications for quantum algorithms and complexity theory.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without introducing additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer tailored optical interactions in a fully optical system to create an effective negative-mass oscillator that coherently cancels quantum backaction.
result: They demonstrate coherent quantum noise cancellation, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a new approach to quantum noise mitigation in hybrid systems, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics in confining systems.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in quantum systems is important for probing confinement in quantum field theories and many-body physics.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize a lattice gauge theory model and study the dynamics of string breaking under adiabatic and diabatic protocols.
result: They observe regimes where string breaking exhibits non-trivial quantum dynamics beyond simple decay, including oscillatory behavior and entanglement generation.
conclusion: The work provides experimental access to complex string-breaking dynamics, offering insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and quantum simulation of gauge theories.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithms.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in quantum processors, especially for near-term devices.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors and use it as a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based quantum processors, aiding in error mitigation.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to many scientific and engineering problems, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods.
result: It provides a taxonomy of algorithms, discusses resource requirements, and surveys applications in machine learning, differential equations, and data fitting.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource constraints.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike.
