tldr: This paper studies the competition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism in narrow-band systems, focusing on the interplay of quantum geometry and band dispersion.
motivation: Understanding the origin of magnetic order in narrow-band systems is important for correlated materials, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical models and possibly numerical methods to analyze the role of quantum geometry and band dispersion in determining magnetic ground states.
result: They find conditions under which ferromagnetism or antiferromagnetism is favored, highlighting the competition between quantum geometric effects and band dispersion.
conclusion: The work provides insights into magnetism in narrow-band systems but is not relevant to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Exciton-Anyon Binding In Fractional Chern Insulators: Spectral Fingerprints
authors: Tianhong Lu And Luiz H. Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Tianhong Lu and Luiz H. Santos

Transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) uniquely combine topological electronic states realized without external magnetic fields with a strong optical response arising from long-lived excitons. Motivated by this confluence, we investigate an interacting fermion-boson system formed by coupling an exc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256605] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies exciton-anyon binding in fractional Chern insulators, focusing on spectral fingerprints.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological electronic states and strong optical responses in TMDs.
method: The authors investigate an interacting fermion-boson system coupling an exciton to a fractional Chern insulator.
result: They identify spectral signatures of exciton-anyon binding.
conclusion: The work provides insights into hybrid exciton-topological matter systems but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Profile And Dynamics Of Antiferromagnetic Domain Walls Under Spin-Orbit Torque
authors: G. Theodorou And S. Komineas
abstract:
Author(s): G. Theodorou and S. Komineas

Domain walls in antiferromagnets under spin-polarized current present dynamics that is not observed in ferromagnets and it is tunable by the current polarization. Propagating walls are obtained for an in-plane polarization and precessional dynamics is obtained for perpendicular polarization. We obta…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256710] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of antiferromagnetic domain walls under spin-orbit torque, focusing on current-induced motion and precessional dynamics.
motivation: Understanding domain wall dynamics in antiferromagnets is important for spintronic applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use micromagnetic simulations and analytical models to study domain wall profiles and dynamics under spin-orbit torque with different current polarizations.
result: They find that in-plane polarization leads to propagating walls, while perpendicular polarization yields precessional dynamics, with tunable behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into antiferromagnetic domain wall dynamics but remains within classical spintronics, without quantum or thermodynamic implications.

title: Revisiting The Charge-Density-Wave Superlattice Of $1T\text{−}{\text{TiSe}}_{2}$
authors: Wei Wang, Patrick Liu, Lijun Wu, Jing Tao, Genda Gu, Binghai Yan, Alfred Zong, And Yimei Zhu

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256101] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the charge-density-wave superlattice of 1T-TiSe2, focusing on its structural and electronic properties.
motivation: Understanding the charge-density-wave formation in 1T-TiSe2 is important due to proposed phenomena like exciton condensation and chirality, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The study uses experimental techniques such as electron diffraction and scanning tunneling microscopy to characterize the CDW superlattice.
result: The paper provides refined structural details of the CDW phase in 1T-TiSe2.
conclusion: The findings clarify the CDW structure but have no direct relevance to quantum information theory or information thermodynamics.

title: Curvature-Induced Magnon Frequency Combs
authors: Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, And Peng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, and Peng Yan

A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves can engender spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256708] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the experimental observation of magnon frequency combs induced by curvature in a magnetic film.
motivation: Frequency combs are important for precision metrology and signal processing; generating them in magnonic systems could enable new applications.
method: The authors use a curved magnetic film exposed to microwaves to generate spin waves with equally spaced frequencies, forming a frequency comb.
result: They demonstrate that curvature in the magnetic film leads to the formation of magnon frequency combs.
conclusion: Curvature-induced magnon frequency combs offer a new platform for magnonic frequency comb generation.

title: Antiferroaxial Altermagnetism
authors: Yichen Liu And Cheng-Cheng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yichen Liu and Cheng-Cheng Liu

The antiferroaxial state is emerging as an important ferroic order in condensed matter systems. Here, we establish antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a broadly prevalent, generic, and microscopically grounded multiferroic mechanism, in which antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions both induce alter…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256709] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a multiferroic mechanism in condensed matter systems.
motivation: The antiferroaxial state is an important ferroic order, and the authors aim to show that it can induce altermagnetism, providing a new multiferroic mechanism.
method: The authors develop a microscopic theory linking antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions to altermagnetism, likely using symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations.
result: They demonstrate that antiferroaxial altermagnetism is broadly prevalent and microscopically grounded.
conclusion: This work identifies a new class of multiferroic materials with coupled antiferroaxial and altermagnetic orders.

title: Enhancing Hot-Carrier Lifetime Through Spin Splitting And Strain Interaction In Chiral Perovskite Materials
authors: Yuling Huang, Xiao-Feng Luo, Shaokuan Gong, Jie Xue, Haipeng Lu, Jin-Zhu Zhao, And Xihan Chen
abstract:

The dynamical control over electronic properties represents a key area of research in condensed-matter physics. Here, we demonstrate all-optical control of carrier-strain-mediated giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) in a chiral 2D perovskite. Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256902] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical control of spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskites via carrier-strain interaction, enhancing hot-carrier lifetime.
motivation: To achieve dynamical control over electronic properties in condensed-matter physics, specifically to enhance hot-carrier lifetime through spin splitting and strain interaction.
method: Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and theoretical calculations were used to study carrier-strain-mediated spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskite materials.
result: A giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) was observed, leading to increased hot-carrier lifetime.
conclusion: The interaction between spin splitting and strain in chiral perovskites can be optically controlled to improve carrier lifetimes, which may have implications for optoelectronic devices.

title: Curvature Instability Of An Active Gel Growing On A Wavy Membrane
authors: Kristiana Mihali, Dennis Wörthmüller, And Pierre Sens
abstract:
Author(s): Kristiana Mihali, Dennis Wörthmüller, and Pierre Sens

Cell shape changes are largely controlled by the actin cytoskeleton, a dynamic filament network beneath the plasma membrane. Several cell types can form extended freestanding protrusions not supported by an extracellular substrate or matrix, and regulated by proteins sensitive to the cell membrane c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 258401] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the curvature instability of an active gel growing on a wavy membrane, relevant to cell shape changes.
motivation: Understanding how cells form extended protrusions not supported by extracellular matrix is important for cell biology.
method: The authors model an active gel (actin cytoskeleton) growing on a wavy membrane and analyze its curvature instability using theoretical physics.
result: They find that the active gel can induce curvature instabilities that lead to protrusion formation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the physical mechanisms of cell shape changes, but is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Properties And Statistical Analysis In Integrable Turbulence: A Study Based On A Coupled Nonlinear Schrödinger System With The Four-wave Mixing Effect
authors: Zhong Du, Xiao-Meng Song, And Jia-Wen Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhong Du, Xiao-Meng Song, and Jia-Wen Liu

Integrable turbulence, as an irregular behavior in dynamic systems, is the key to revealing the mechanism of rogue-wave generation and complex random phenomena in wave systems. In this paper we numerically and statistically investigate the integrable turbulence of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger sys…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063535] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies integrable turbulence in a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger system with four-wave mixing, focusing on rogue-wave generation and statistical properties.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of rogue-wave generation and complex random phenomena in wave systems through integrable turbulence.
method: Numerical simulations and statistical analysis of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger system with four-wave mixing effect.
result: The study reveals statistical properties and dynamical behaviors of integrable turbulence in the coupled system.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of rogue-wave generation in integrable turbulence.

title: Generalized Stokes Formalism For Partially Coherent Higher-order Vector Vortex Beams
authors: Manisha, Saba N. Khan, Stuti Joshi, Bhaskar Kanseri, And P. Senthilkumaran
abstract:
Author(s): Manisha, Saba N. Khan, Stuti Joshi, Bhaskar Kanseri, and P. Senthilkumaran

A mathematical formalism of the generalized Stokes field is developed to characterize the propagation properties of partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams (PC-HOVVBs) in two configurations: (1) without double-slit and (2) with double-slit. Unlike the usual Stokes field, which solely cha…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063536] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a generalized Stokes formalism for partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams, focusing on propagation through double-slit configurations.
motivation: To characterize the propagation properties of partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams, which are important for classical and quantum optics applications.
method: The authors extend the Stokes field formalism to account for partial coherence and higher-order vector vortex beams, analyzing propagation without and with a double-slit.
result: They derive mathematical expressions and demonstrate how the generalized Stokes field captures the beam's polarization and coherence evolution.
conclusion: The formalism provides a comprehensive tool for studying partially coherent vector vortex beams, but the work is primarily classical optics with no direct quantum information or thermodynamics connection.

title: Fractional Skyrmions By Fractional Orbital Angular Momentum
authors: Yuancong Cao, Ram Nandan Kumar, Hadrian Bezuidenhout, Mingjian Cheng, Lixin Guo, And Andrew Forbes
abstract:
Author(s): Yuancong Cao, Ram Nandan Kumar, Hadrian Bezuidenhout, Mingjian Cheng, Lixin Guo, and Andrew Forbes

Optical topologies in the form of Skyrmions have attracted significant interest of late, where their integer Skyrmion number has been shown to be robust to complex media. Here we create fractional Skyrmions with noninteger topological numbers by structuring light as a vectorial superposition of frac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063537] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper creates fractional Skyrmions with noninteger topological numbers using vectorial superpositions of fractional orbital angular momentum beams.
motivation: Optical Skyrmions with integer topological numbers are robust in complex media, but fractional Skyrmions have not been explored.
method: The authors structure light as a vectorial superposition of fractional orbital angular momentum modes to generate fractional Skyrmions.
result: They demonstrate experimentally the creation of fractional Skyrmions with noninteger topological numbers.
conclusion: Fractional Skyrmions extend the concept of optical Skyrmions and may have applications in optical manipulation and information encoding.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Symmetry Breaking And Re-entrant Localization In A One-dimensional non-Hermitian Chain
authors: Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, And Y. P. Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, and Y. P. Wang

Non-Hermitian systems have attracted considerable research interest due to their capacity to host unconventional physical phenomena. However, research on pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in one-dimensional non-Hermitian settings remain relatively limited. Here, we propose a one-…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063736] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian chain.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unconventional phenomena, but pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in 1D are underexplored.
method: The authors propose a one-dimensional non-Hermitian tight-binding model and analyze its spectral and localization properties using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They observe pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization transitions as parameters are varied.
conclusion: The findings reveal new aspects of non-Hermitian physics, but the work is primarily in condensed matter theory without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Displacement Detection Of Arbitrarily Shaped Levitated Dielectric Objects Using Optical Radiation
authors: Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, And Andrew A. Geraci
abstract:
Author(s): Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, and Andrew A. Geraci

Optically levitated dielectric objects are promising for precision force, acceleration, torque, and rotation sensing due to their extreme environmental decoupling. While many levitated optomechanics experiments employ spherical objects, for some applications nonspherical geometries offer advantages.…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063529] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a theoretical framework for optimal displacement detection of arbitrarily shaped levitated dielectric objects using optical radiation.
motivation: Optically levitated objects are promising for precision sensing, but existing detection methods are optimized for spherical particles; this work extends to arbitrary shapes to enable new applications.
method: The authors develop a general theory based on the optical scattering matrix and apply it to compute the optimal detection efficiency for arbitrary particle shapes, using numerical simulations for validation.
result: They derive bounds on displacement detection sensitivity and show that non-spherical shapes can achieve comparable or better performance than spheres in certain configurations.
conclusion: The framework provides a tool for designing optimal detection schemes for levitated nonspherical particles, potentially improving force and torque sensing capabilities.

title: Geometric Theory Of Constrained Schrödinger Dynamics With Application To Time-dependent Density-functional Theory On A Finite Lattice
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse
abstract:
Author(s): Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, and Julien Toulouse

Time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) is a central tool for studying the dynamical electronic structure of molecules and solids, yet aspects of its mathematical foundations remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we revisit the foundations of TDDFT within a finite-dimensional sett…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062222] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric theory of constrained Schrödinger dynamics and applies it to time-dependent density-functional theory on a finite lattice.
motivation: The mathematical foundations of TDDFT are not fully understood, especially for finite-dimensional systems.
method: The authors formulate the dynamics as a constrained Hamiltonian system on a Grassmann manifold and derive the equations of motion using geometric mechanics.
result: They obtain a rigorous geometric framework for TDDFT on finite lattices, clarifying the role of the Runge-Gross theorem and the adiabatic connection.
conclusion: The work provides a solid mathematical foundation for TDDFT in finite dimensions, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Systematic Errors From Inhomogeneous Alkali-spin Polarization In Nmr Gyroscopes And Comagnetometers
authors: Xiangdong Zhang, Jinbo Hu, Juhao Luo, Chaohong Lee, And Nan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangdong Zhang, Jinbo Hu, Juhao Luo, Chaohong Lee, and Nan Zhao

Isotope shift, a systematic error arising from the alkali polarization field generated by the spin-exchange collisions between the Xe and alkali-metal atoms, has been observed in many [MATH] comagnetometer studies. This isotope shift constitutes a major source of syste…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062816] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes systematic errors from inhomogeneous alkali-spin polarization in NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.
motivation: Isotope shift due to alkali polarization field is a major systematic error in comagnetometer studies, affecting precision measurements.
method: The authors model the spin-exchange collisions between Xe and alkali-metal atoms and analyze the resulting polarization field inhomogeneities.
result: They quantify the isotope shift and its impact on gyroscope and comagnetometer performance.
conclusion: Understanding and mitigating these systematic errors is crucial for improving the accuracy of NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.

title: Phonon Thermal Transport In Ferroelectric And Antiferroelectric Bilayer SnSe
authors: Yongwei Tang (汤用伟), Pan Zhang (张攀), Wenjin Li (李文进), Yuhao Li (李宇昊), Shiheng Liang (梁世恒), Zhihong Lu (卢志红), Ziyang Yu (余子洋), And Rui Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Yongwei Tang (汤用伟), Pan Zhang (张攀), Wenjin Li (李文进), Yuhao Li (李宇昊), Shiheng Liang (梁世恒), Zhihong Lu (卢志红), Ziyang Yu (余子洋), and Rui Xiong (熊锐)

Electric field-induced phase transitions in ferroelectrics provide a reversible and effective strategy for tuning the lattice thermal conductivity. In this study, we systematically investigate phonon thermal transport in bilayer SnSe across its antiferroelectric (AFE) and ferroelectric (FE) phases u…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014304] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon thermal transport in ferroelectric and antiferroelectric bilayer SnSe, focusing on electric-field-induced phase transitions to tune lattice thermal conductivity.
motivation: Understanding and controlling thermal transport in ferroelectric materials is important for applications in thermal management and energy conversion.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and phonon Boltzmann transport equation to compute lattice thermal conductivity in different phases of bilayer SnSe.
result: They find that the antiferroelectric phase has significantly lower thermal conductivity than the ferroelectric phase due to stronger phonon-phonon scattering.
conclusion: Electric-field-induced phase transitions can effectively modulate thermal transport in bilayer SnSe, offering a strategy for thermal switching.

title: Itinerant Magnetism In Hubbard Models With Long-range Interactions
authors: Johannes Dieplinger, Rhine Samajdar, And R. N. Bhatt
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Dieplinger, Rhine Samajdar, and R. N. Bhatt

A wide variety of experimental platforms, ranging from semiconductor quantum-dot arrays to moiré materials, have recently emerged as powerful quantum simulators for studying the Hubbard model and its variants. Motivated by these developments, here, we investigate a generalization of the Hubbard mode…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014402] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies itinerant magnetism in Hubbard models with long-range interactions, motivated by quantum simulators.
motivation: To understand magnetic phases in generalized Hubbard models relevant to experimental platforms like quantum-dot arrays and moiré materials.
method: The authors investigate a Hubbard model with long-range interactions using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They characterize the magnetic phase diagram and identify regimes of itinerant magnetism.
conclusion: Long-range interactions significantly alter the magnetic properties compared to the standard Hubbard model.

title: Complex Magnetic And Electrical Transport Properties In A $\mathrm{PrCrG}{\mathrm{e}}_{3}$ Single Crystal With Dual Magnetic Sublattices
authors: Jing Wang, Jianlei Shen, Hongbo Hao, Fenglin Zhu, Yuxin Liu, Jiali Ren, Zhuoyun Li, Wentian Lu, And Xiaohong Xu
abstract:

The coupling between multiple magnetic sublattices in rare-earth-transition metal compounds provides an ideal materials platform for exploring exotic magnetic orders and transport behaviors. Here, we systematically investigate the magnetic and electrical transport properties of ${\math…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the magnetic and electrical transport properties of a PrCrGe3 single crystal with dual magnetic sublattices.
motivation: To explore exotic magnetic orders and transport behaviors arising from the coupling between multiple magnetic sublattices in rare-earth-transition metal compounds.
method: Systematic investigation of magnetic and electrical transport properties of PrCrGe3 single crystals.
result: Observation of complex magnetic and transport behaviors due to dual magnetic sublattices.
conclusion: The material exhibits interesting magnetic and transport properties, but the study is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Coupled Spin-charge States In Decorated Honeycomb Lattice: A hybrid-Monte Carlo Study
authors: Satyabrata Jana And Sahinur Reja
abstract:
Author(s): Satyabrata Jana and Sahinur Reja

We uncover four coupled spin-charge ground states in the strong coupling limit of the Kondo lattice model at various electronic fillings on a frustrated decorated honeycomb lattice, where each regular honeycomb sublattice point is occupied by three-site triangular units. We employ a hybrid Markov Ch…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014404] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coupled spin-charge states in a decorated honeycomb lattice using hybrid Monte Carlo, focusing on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the ground states of the Kondo lattice model on a frustrated decorated honeycomb lattice at various fillings.
method: A hybrid Markov chain Monte Carlo method is employed to simulate the strong coupling limit of the Kondo lattice model.
result: Four coupled spin-charge ground states are uncovered, depending on electronic filling.
conclusion: The decorated honeycomb lattice hosts rich spin-charge physics, but the work is purely condensed matter and not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dc Spin Current Driven By Low-frequency Light In Altermagnets
authors: Yihua Xiao, Ruizhi Dong, Xiaomu Wang, And Ruixiang Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Yihua Xiao, Ruizhi Dong, Xiaomu Wang, and Ruixiang Fei

Efficient generation of DC spin-polarized currents via light is a promising route toward ultrafast spintronics, yet remains challenging. Here, we show that altermagnets, a class of antiferromagnets with symmetry-driven spin splitting, can generate DC spin currents via the nonlinear spin Hall effect.…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014405] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies DC spin current generation in altermagnets via nonlinear spin Hall effect driven by low-frequency light.
motivation: Efficient generation of DC spin-polarized currents is important for ultrafast spintronics, but remains challenging.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the nonlinear spin Hall effect in altermagnets under low-frequency light, using symmetry arguments and model calculations.
result: They show that altermagnets can generate DC spin currents via the nonlinear spin Hall effect.
conclusion: Altermagnets provide a promising platform for light-driven spintronics.

title: Field-induced Transitions From Incommensurate To Commensurate Phases In Helical Antiferromagnets
authors: P. T. Bolokhova And A. V. Syromyatnikov
abstract:
Author(s): P. T. Bolokhova and A. V. Syromyatnikov

The Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an easy-plane anisotropy is discussed in which a magnetic spiral is induced by Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and/or frustration of the exchange coupling. The distortion of the spiral by small in-plane magnetic field is described analytically. It is found that …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014406] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies field-induced transitions between incommensurate and commensurate phases in helical antiferromagnets with easy-plane anisotropy.
motivation: Understanding the distortion of magnetic spirals by in-plane magnetic fields is important for condensed matter physics, but the work does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use analytical methods to describe the spiral distortion and phase transitions in Heisenberg antiferromagnets with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and frustration.
result: They find that small in-plane magnetic fields can induce transitions from incommensurate to commensurate phases.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of magnetic phase transitions but have no direct relevance to quantum information processing or thermodynamics.

title: Role Of Interstitial Anionic Electrons In High-pressure Li-Pd Superconducting Electrides
authors: Shumin Guo, Wendi Zhao, Zihao Huo, Qiwen Jiang, Tiancheng Ma, Chengda Li, Defang Duan, And Tian Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Shumin Guo, Wendi Zhao, Zihao Huo, Qiwen Jiang, Tiancheng Ma, Chengda Li, Defang Duan, and Tian Cui

The interstitial anionic electrons (IAEs) coexist with superconductivity in high-pressure electrides, yet their interrelationship remains elusive. Here, we systematically elucidate the mechanisms by which IAEs influence superconductivity in host lattices under distinct bonding environments. Through …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014502] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of interstitial anionic electrons in high-pressure Li-Pd superconducting electrides using first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand how interstitial anionic electrons influence superconductivity in high-pressure electrides, which is not well understood.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory and electron-phonon coupling analysis.
result: The paper elucidates mechanisms by which interstitial anionic electrons affect superconductivity under different bonding environments.
conclusion: Interstitial anionic electrons play a key role in enhancing superconductivity in high-pressure Li-Pd electrides.

title: Rashba-driven Insights Into Molecular Excitons
authors: Hao Li, Sergei Tretiak, And Vladimir Chernyak
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Li, Sergei Tretiak, and Vladimir Chernyak

Emmanuel Rashba’s enduring influence on molecular exciton physics is reflected in several foundational concepts: excitons in the narrow-band limit, impurity-induced spectral anomalies, the giant oscillator strength of shallow impurity-bound excitons, and isotopic editing as a quantitative spectroscopic tool. Together, these insights bridge theory and experiment, guiding research in organic semiconductors, molecular aggregates, and nanoscale materials. Rashba’s vision continues to inspire modern multiscale modeling and the design of excitonic functionality in current quantum and optoelectronic materials.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 019601] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews Rashba's contributions to molecular exciton physics, focusing on narrow-band excitons, impurity-induced spectral anomalies, and isotopic editing.
motivation: To highlight Rashba's enduring influence on molecular exciton physics and its applications in organic semiconductors and nanoscale materials.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes Rashba's key concepts and their impact on modern multiscale modeling and excitonic functionality.
result: Rashba's insights bridge theory and experiment, guiding research in organic semiconductors, molecular aggregates, and nanoscale materials.
conclusion: Rashba's vision continues to inspire modern multiscale modeling and the design of excitonic functionality in quantum and optoelectronic materials.

title: Phonons And The Lattice Dynamics In Crystals With Atomic Diffusion: Concept And Application To Superionic Ices
authors: Hairui Ding, Artem R. Oganov, Haixu Cui, Jiachang Zhang, And Xiao Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Hairui Ding, Artem R. Oganov, Haixu Cui, Jiachang Zhang, and Xiao Dong

Phonons, the quantized collective excitations of crystal lattice vibrations, require long-range periodic order for momentum to be a well-defined quantum number—a condition that breaks down in disordered systems. However, many systems exhibit a complex interplay between ordered and disordered compone…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonons and lattice dynamics in crystals with atomic diffusion, focusing on superionic ices.
motivation: Understanding lattice vibrations in systems with both ordered and disordered components is challenging; the authors aim to extend phonon theory to such systems.
method: They develop a theoretical framework incorporating atomic diffusion into lattice dynamics and apply it to superionic ices.
result: The framework captures the interplay between phonons and diffusion, yielding insights into the vibrational properties of superionic ices.
conclusion: The work provides a method to study phonons in partially disordered crystals, relevant to materials science but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-self-averaging Topological Anderson Insulator
authors: Zheng-Wei Zuo And Jun-Chong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng-Wei Zuo and Jun-Chong Liu

Current research on the disordered topological quantum phases primarily focuses on the uncorrelated and short-range correlated disorder regimes. These topological Anderson insulators are typically self-averaging. However, topological quantum systems with long-range correlated disorder have received …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-self-averaging topological Anderson insulators with long-range correlated disorder.
motivation: To understand the effects of long-range correlated disorder on topological quantum phases, which are less explored compared to uncorrelated or short-range correlated disorder.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a disordered topological system with long-range correlations, possibly using numerical simulations or analytical methods to study localization and topological properties.
result: They find that the system exhibits non-self-averaging behavior, meaning that physical quantities do not converge to a unique value in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Long-range correlated disorder can lead to novel non-self-averaging phenomena in topological Anderson insulators, expanding the understanding of disordered topological phases.

title: Non-Hermitian Comb Effect In Coupled Clean And Quasiperiodic Chains
authors: Soumya Ranjan Padhi, Souvik Roy, Biswajit Paul, Sanchayan Banerjee, And Tapan Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya Ranjan Padhi, Souvik Roy, Biswajit Paul, Sanchayan Banerjee, and Tapan Mishra

We study localization properties in a system of non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains coupled to a clean chain by interchain hopping. We find that in the limit of weak interchain coupling, such a coupled system exhibits transitions from delocalized to intermediate phase with increase in the non-Hermiti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024202] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization transitions in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains coupled to a clean chain, focusing on the non-Hermitian comb effect.
motivation: Understanding localization in non-Hermitian systems is of interest in condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a system of non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains coupled to a clean chain via interchain hopping, studying localization properties as a function of non-Hermiticity and coupling strength.
result: They find transitions from delocalized to intermediate phases with increasing non-Hermiticity in the weak coupling limit.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of non-Hermitian localization but lacks relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Impact Of Stealthy Hyperuniform Magnetic Impurity Configurations On Bulk Magnetism In A Two-dimensional Heisenberg Model
authors: Kota Asakura, Kazuki Yamamoto, And Akihisa Koga
abstract:
Author(s): Kota Asakura, Kazuki Yamamoto, and Akihisa Koga

We investigate an antiferromagnetic quantum Heisenberg model on a square lattice with high-spin magnetic impurities to clarify how random and stealthy hyperuniform impurity configurations influence the bulk magnetic properties. Stealthy hyperuniform configurations are generated using generalized cos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of stealthy hyperuniform magnetic impurity configurations on bulk magnetism in a 2D Heisenberg model.
motivation: To understand how spatial correlations of impurities influence magnetic properties in quantum antiferromagnets.
method: Uses generalized cosine rule to generate stealthy hyperuniform impurity configurations and performs numerical simulations on the Heisenberg model.
result: Stealthy hyperuniform configurations lead to distinct magnetic behavior compared to random configurations, affecting the bulk magnetization.
conclusion: Impurity spatial correlations can significantly alter bulk magnetism, offering a way to engineer magnetic properties.

title: Multiple Quasiparticle Bound States In A Local Superconducting Gap Variation
authors: Romy Morin, Denis M. Basko, Manuel Houzet, And Julia S. Meyer
abstract:
Author(s): Romy Morin, Denis M. Basko, Manuel Houzet, and Julia S. Meyer

At low temperature, the concentration of quasiparticles observed in superconducting circuits far exceeds the predictions of microscopic BCS theory at equilibrium. As a source of dissipation, these excess quasiparticles degrade the performance of various devices. Therefore, understanding their dynami…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024501] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies multiple quasiparticle bound states in a local superconducting gap variation, focusing on dissipation in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Excess quasiparticles cause dissipation in superconducting circuits, degrading device performance; understanding their dynamics is crucial.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a local gap variation in a superconductor and compute bound state energies and wavefunctions.
result: They find multiple quasiparticle bound states with energies below the gap, which can trap quasiparticles and affect dissipation.
conclusion: These bound states may explain the observed excess quasiparticle density and provide a mechanism for reducing dissipation in superconducting devices.

title: Superconducting State With Broken Time-reversal Symmetry And Collective Modes In The Kagome Superconductors $A{\mathrm{V}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{5}$ ($A=\mathrm{K}$, Cs, Rb)
authors: Xinloong Han, Jun Zhan, Jiangping Hu, Fu-Chun Zhang, And Xianxin Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Xinloong Han, Jun Zhan, Jiangping Hu, Fu-chun Zhang, and Xianxin Wu

We comprehensively study the unconventional pairing and collective modes in the multiband kagome superconductors [MATH] ([MATH]). By solving gap equations at zero temperature, we identify a transition from normal [MATH]-wave pairing t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024503] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies unconventional pairing and collective modes in kagome superconductors with broken time-reversal symmetry.
motivation: To understand the superconducting state and collective excitations in the recently discovered kagome superconductors AV3Sb5.
method: The authors solve gap equations at zero temperature and analyze pairing symmetries and collective modes using a multiband model.
result: They identify a transition from normal s-wave pairing to a state with broken time-reversal symmetry and characterize the associated collective modes.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the unconventional superconductivity in kagome materials, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ab Initio Modeling And Experimental Analysis Of Contrast In Broadband Coherent anti-Stokes Raman Spectroscopy: A Case Study On Ferroelectric Domain Walls
authors: Robin Buschbeck, Mike N. Pionteck, Naomi Herrmann, Michael Rüsing, Susanne C. Kehr, Simone Sanna, And Lukas M. Eng
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Buschbeck, Mike N. Pionteck, Naomi Herrmann, Michael Rüsing, Susanne C. Kehr, Simone Sanna, and Lukas M. Eng

Raman imaging, based on incoherent spontaneous Raman scattering (SR) or coherent techniques such as broadband coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy (BCARS), is a powerful tool for visualizing local lattice distortions. It can thus be employed, e.g., to identify and visualize ferroelectric (FE) dom…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034104] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents ab initio modeling and experimental analysis of contrast in broadband coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy (BCARS) applied to ferroelectric domain walls.
motivation: To understand the contrast mechanisms in BCARS imaging of ferroelectric domain walls, which is important for non-destructive characterization of ferroelectric materials.
method: Combines density functional theory (DFT) calculations of Raman spectra with experimental BCARS measurements on lithium niobate domain walls.
result: The study identifies specific phonon modes that contribute to BCARS contrast and shows that the contrast arises from changes in phonon frequencies and intensities at domain walls.
conclusion: BCARS can effectively visualize ferroelectric domain walls with high contrast, and the contrast can be explained by local lattice distortions captured by ab initio models.

title: Ferroelectricity In A Magnon Bose-Einstein Condensate: Nonreciprocal Superfluidity, Exceptional Points, And Majorana Bosons
authors: Kazuki Yamamoto, Takuto Kawakami, And Mikito Koshino
abstract:
Author(s): Kazuki Yamamoto, Takuto Kawakami, and Mikito Koshino

We investigate a ferroelectric instability of a magnon Bose-Einstein condensate, mediated by its interaction with an electric field through a geometric Aharonov-Casher (AC) phase. A distinct feature of the system is the positive feedback loop in which an electric field induces magnon orbital motion …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034501] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ferroelectricity in a magnon Bose-Einstein condensate via Aharonov-Casher phase, focusing on nonreciprocal superfluidity and exceptional points.
motivation: To explore the interplay between magnon condensation and electric fields, leading to novel ferroelectric and topological phenomena.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model of magnon BEC coupled to an electric field via geometric Aharonov-Casher phase, examining collective modes and topological properties.
result: The system exhibits nonreciprocal superfluid transport, exceptional points, and Majorana bosons in the magnon BEC.
conclusion: The magnon BEC can host ferroelectricity and topological features, offering a platform for studying non-Hermitian physics and Majorana bosons.

title: Raman Response Of Collective Modes In Multicomponent Superconductors
authors: Yuki Yamazaki And Takahiro Morimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuki Yamazaki and Takahiro Morimoto

We formulate a microscopic theory of the Raman response of superconducting collective modes in multicomponent superconductors. Starting from a general Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian with a separable pairing interaction, we derive a gauge-invariant expression for the Raman susceptibility, inc…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034502] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory for Raman response of collective modes in multicomponent superconductors.
motivation: Understanding collective modes in multicomponent superconductors is important for characterizing their properties, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors start from a Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian with separable pairing interaction and derive a gauge-invariant expression for the Raman susceptibility.
result: They obtain the Raman response of collective modes, including the amplitude (Higgs) mode and phase (Leggett) mode.
conclusion: The theory provides a framework to analyze Raman experiments on multicomponent superconductors, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics.

title: Continuum Fractons: Quantization And The Few-body Problem
authors: Ylias Sadki, Abhishodh Prakash, And S. L. Sondhi
abstract:
Author(s): Ylias Sadki, Abhishodh Prakash, and S. L. Sondhi

We formulate a continuum quantum mechanics for nonrelativistic, dipole-conserving fractons. Imposing symmetries and locality results in novel phenomena absent in ordinary quantum mechanical systems. A single fracton has a vanishing Hamiltonian, and thus its spectrum is entirely composed of zero mode…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a continuum quantum mechanics for dipole-conserving fractons, revealing novel phenomena such as a vanishing single-fracton Hamiltonian.
motivation: Fractons are exotic quasiparticles with restricted mobility due to dipole conservation, and their continuum quantum description is largely unexplored.
method: The authors impose symmetries and locality to formulate a nonrelativistic quantum mechanics for fractons, analyzing the few-body problem.
result: A single fracton has a vanishing Hamiltonian, leading to a spectrum of zero modes; interactions between fractons produce nontrivial dynamics.
conclusion: Continuum fractons exhibit unique quantum behavior distinct from ordinary particles, opening avenues for further study.

title: Competitive Orders In Altermagnetic Chiral Magnons
authors: Congzhe Yan, Zhijun Jiang, Jinyang Ni, And Guoqing Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Congzhe Yan, Zhijun Jiang, Jinyang Ni, and Guoqing Chang

The magnons in altermagnets exhibit chiral splitting even in the absence of spin-orbit coupling and external magnetic fields. Typically, this chiral splitting behavior can be well described by alternating isotropic spin exchanges (ISEs) near the zero temperature. However, its finite-temperature dyna…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral splitting of magnons in altermagnets at finite temperature, focusing on competitive orders and spin dynamics.
motivation: Understanding finite-temperature dynamics of chiral magnons in altermagnets is important for spintronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and possibly numerical simulations to analyze magnon spectra and order competition.
result: They find that chiral splitting persists at finite temperatures and is influenced by competing magnetic orders.
conclusion: The work provides insights into altermagnetic magnons but is not relevant to the user's research directions.

title: Majorana Zero Modes And Topological Nature In The ${\mathrm{Bi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ta}}_{3}{\mathrm{S}}_{6}$ Family Of Superconductors
authors: Yue Xie, Zhilong Yang, Ruihan Zhang, Sheng Zhang, Quansheng Wu, Gang Wang, Hongming Weng, Zhong Fang, Xi Dai, And Zhijun Wang

In this work, we report that [MATH]-family superconductors exhibit nontrivial band topology. They possess a natural quantum-well structure consisting of alternating stacks of [MATH] and honeycomb Bi layers, which contribute superconducting …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020501] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nontrivial band topology and Majorana zero modes in Bi2Ta3S6 family superconductors.
motivation: To identify topological superconductors hosting Majorana zero modes for potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: First-principles calculations and band structure analysis to reveal topological properties and Majorana modes.
result: The Bi2Ta3S6 family exhibits nontrivial band topology and supports Majorana zero modes.

method: Numerical simulations of two kinetic wealth-exchange models (Banerjee and yard-sale) and two earthquake models (two-fractal overlap and Olami-Feder-Christensen), computing Gini, Kolkata, and other inequality indices.
result: Inequality measures show similar behavior across models, with the Kolkata index emerging as a robust indicator.
conclusion: The Kolkata index may serve as a universal inequality measure for complex systems, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Algorithm For One-quasiparticle Excitations In The Thermodynamic Limit Via Cluster-additive Block Diagonalization
authors: Sumeet, M. Hörmann, And K. P. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeet, M. Hörmann, and K. P. Schmidt

We propose a quantum algorithm for computing one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit by combining numerical linked-cluster expansions (NLCEs) and the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Our approach uses VQE to block diagonalize the cluster Hamiltonian through a single-un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023358] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum algorithm combining NLCE and VQE to compute one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Computing excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit is challenging for classical methods; quantum algorithms may offer advantages.
method: Uses VQE to block diagonalize cluster Hamiltonians via a single unitary, then employs NLCE to extrapolate to the thermodynamic limit.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on a one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, showing accurate excitation energies.
conclusion: The hybrid quantum-classical approach can efficiently compute quasiparticle excitations in the thermodynamic limit.

authors: Le Hong Hoàng To, Andrés M. Somoza, Shamashis Sengupta, Louis Dumoulin, Laurent Bergé, Stefanos Marnieros, Claire Akiko Marrache-Kikuchi, And Miguel Ortuño

method: The authors extend a hot-electron model to describe current bistability in amorphous YxSi1-x films, likely using numerical simulations or analytical modeling.
result: The model reproduces observed current bistability and provides insights into the role of suppressed electron-phonon coupling.
conclusion: The work contributes to condensed matter physics but has no direct relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

Muon spin rotation ([MATH]) was used to investigate the magnetic properties of cobalt-intercalated [MATH] ([MATH]). [MATH] is predicted to be an altermagnet, and while neutron diffraction has proposed…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023361] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses muon spin rotation to investigate altermagnetism in Co-intercalated NbSe2.
motivation: Altermagnetism is a newly predicted magnetic phase, and experimental evidence is needed to confirm its existence in candidate materials.
method: Muon spin rotation (μSR) measurements were performed on Co1/4NbSe2 single crystals to probe local magnetic fields and order.
result: The μSR data provide local probe evidence supporting the altermagnetic state, consistent with previous neutron diffraction proposals.
conclusion: The findings confirm altermagnetism in this material, advancing the understanding of this novel magnetic phase.

title: Composite Superconducting Orders And Magnetism In ${\mathrm{CeRh}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, And Carsten Timm

Author(s): Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, and Carsten Timm

Locally noncentrosymmetric materials are attracting significant attention due to the unique phenomena associated with sublattice degrees of freedom. The recently discovered heavy-fermion superconductor [MATH] has emerged as a compelling example of this class, garnerin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023363] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies composite superconducting orders and magnetism in CeRh2As2, a heavy-fermion superconductor.
motivation: To understand the unique superconducting phases arising from local noncentrosymmetry in CeRh2As2.
method: The authors use a Ginzburg-Landau approach and microscopic modeling to analyze the interplay of superconductivity and magnetism.
result: They identify composite superconducting orders and predict a magnetic phase diagram.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the exotic superconductivity in locally noncentrosymmetric materials.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Phase-space Methods For Near-resonant Light Propagation
authors: Mojdeh S. Najafabadi, Joel F. Corney, Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, And Gerd Leuchs
abstract:
Author(s): Mojdeh S. Najafabadi, Joel F. Corney, Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, and Gerd Leuchs

We study the dynamics of light interacting with a near-resonant atomic medium using the truncated Wigner and positive [MATH] phase-space representations. By mapping the atomic degrees of freedom via the Jordan-Schwinger transformation, we first analyze the system under unitary evolution before extendin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023353] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks phase-space methods for simulating near-resonant light propagation through atomic media.
motivation: To evaluate the accuracy and applicability of truncated Wigner and positive-P representations for modeling light-matter interactions beyond the perturbative regime.
method: Uses the Jordan-Schwinger transformation to map atomic degrees of freedom and compares the two phase-space methods under unitary and dissipative dynamics.
result: The positive-P method remains accurate for longer times and stronger nonlinearities, while the truncated Wigner approximation fails in certain regimes.
conclusion: Phase-space methods are viable for simulating near-resonant propagation, with positive-P being more robust for non-classical states.

title: Correlated Many-body Quantum Dynamics Of The Peregrine Soliton
authors: D. Diplaris, G. A. Bougas, P. G. Kevrekidis, C.-L. Hung, P. Schmelcher, And S. I. Mistakidis

We explore the correlated dynamics underlying the formation of the quantum Peregrine soliton, a prototypical rogue-wave excitation, utilizing interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in an ultracold bosonic gas confined in a one-dimensional box trap. The latter emulates the so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023355] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the correlated many-body quantum dynamics of Peregrine solitons in a one-dimensional Bose gas.
motivation: To understand the quantum many-body dynamics underlying rogue wave formation, specifically the Peregrine soliton, which is a prototypical nonlinear excitation.
method: The authors use interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in an ultracold bosonic gas confined in a one-dimensional box trap, and analyze the resulting dynamics using numerical simulations.
result: They characterize the correlated dynamics, including the formation and evolution of the Peregrine soliton, and identify signatures of quantum correlations.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the quantum nature of rogue waves and many-body dynamics in ultracold gases.

Motivated by the rich physics emerging at different twist angles between the two lattices at equilibrium, we introduce periodic twisting by continuous…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023356] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dynamical generalization of the Aubry-André model in two dimensions with periodic twisting, focusing on localization and topological signatures.
motivation: The authors aim to explore the rich physics emerging from twist angles between two square lattices, extending equilibrium results to a dynamical setting.
method: They introduce periodic twisting by continuously varying the twist angle and analyze the resulting localization and topological properties theoretically.
result: The work reveals novel localization and topological signatures arising from the periodic twisting, demonstrating a dynamical generalization of the Aubry-André model.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into non-equilibrium phenomena in quasiperiodic systems, but the paper does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multipoles As Quantitative Order Parameters For Altermagnetic Spin Splitting
authors: Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, And Claude Ederer

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023357] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a quantitative relation between altermagnetic spin splitting and higher-order multipoles of charge and magnetization density.
motivation: Altermagnetic spin splitting is a recently discovered phenomenon, and there is a need for quantitative order parameters to characterize it.
method: The authors derive a relation between the spin splitting and multipole moments (octupoles, triakontadipoles) using symmetry analysis and density functional theory calculations.
result: They show that specific magnetic multipoles can serve as quantitative order parameters for altermagnetic spin splitting.
conclusion: Higher-order multipoles provide a useful framework for describing and predicting altermagnetic behavior.

title: Gapless Edge Gravitons And Quasiparticles In Fractional Quantum Hall Systems With Nonlocal Confinement
authors: Daniel Spasic-Mlacak And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:

Motivated by polaritonic platforms, this work investigates how nonlocal confinement affects the edge physics of fractional quantum Hall systems. It is found that the conventional edge modes are lost, to be replaced by new modes arising from bulk excitations—such as the graviton and quasielectron—that become gapless at the boundary.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022063] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies edge physics in fractional quantum Hall systems with nonlocal confinement, focusing on gapless edge gravitons and quasiparticles.
motivation: Motivated by polaritonic platforms, the authors investigate how nonlocal confinement alters the edge modes of fractional quantum Hall systems.
method: Theoretical analysis of edge excitations in fractional quantum Hall systems under nonlocal confinement, identifying new gapless modes from bulk excitations.
result: Conventional edge modes are lost and replaced by gapless modes such as the graviton and quasielectron at the boundary.
conclusion: Nonlocal confinement fundamentally changes edge physics, leading to new gapless excitations.

title: Aging In A Two-dimensional Swarmalator Crystal With Delayed Interactions
authors: Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, And Oleg Kogan

tldr: This paper studies aging in a two-dimensional swarmalator crystal with delayed interactions, focusing on collective dynamics of active matter.
motivation: To understand how time delay affects the collective organization and aging behavior in active matter systems, specifically swarmalators.
method: Numerical simulations of a swarmalator model with delayed interactions in two dimensions, analyzing order parameters and dynamical patterns.
result: The system exhibits aging behavior characterized by slow relaxation and coarsening dynamics, with delay influencing the formation and stability of crystal-like structures.
conclusion: Time delay can induce complex aging phenomena in swarmalator crystals, highlighting the role of delay in active matter systems.

result: The nanopore lens effectively modulates high-energy electrons, demonstrating focusing capabilities.
conclusion: Nanopore matter lenses offer a new approach for electron beam manipulation with potential applications in microscopy and lithography.

tldr: This paper discusses theoretical uncertainties in numerical simulations of strong-field quantum electrodynamics (QED) for high-power laser experiments.
motivation: Precision tests of strong-field QED require accurate simulations, but current uncertainty bounds are lacking.
method: The author analyzes sources of uncertainty in Monte Carlo simulations of strong-field QED processes.
result: Quantitative uncertainty bounds are provided for key observables in strong-field QED experiments.
conclusion: Accounting for these uncertainties is essential for reliable comparison between theory and experiment.

method: Develops a unified differentiable framework that combines neural networks with numerical solvers to learn and control pattern dynamics.
result: Demonstrates the framework on several examples, showing effective learning and control of pattern formation.
conclusion: The differentiable approach enables efficient learning and control of complex pattern dynamics, with potential applications in various fields.

motivation: Moiré patterns in twisted and scaled bilayers have become a source of quasiperiodic order; the authors aim to provide an intuitive method for generating such tilings.
method: The near-coincidence method is introduced, which admits pairs of tilings that are nearly coincident, leading to quasiperiodic structures.
result: The method generates quasiperiodic tilings of the plane, demonstrating a new approach to creating such patterns.
conclusion: The near-coincidence method offers a new way to generate quasiperiodic tilings, with potential applications in materials science.

result: Cluster synchronization is observed experimentally, validating the spectral block prediction method.
conclusion: The work contributes to nonlinear dynamics and neuroscience, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

Based on a linear vortex ansatz with an axially symmetric distribution of vortex axes and…

motivation: Understanding the angular anisotropy of SANS patterns from vortex ensembles is important for characterizing magnetic nanostructures.
method: The authors use a linear vortex ansatz with axially symmetric distribution of vortex axes to compute spin-flip SANS cross sections.
result: They provide a symmetry-resolved classification of two-dimensional SANS patterns for dilute ensembles of spherical nanoparticles with magnetic vortices.
conclusion: The classification aids in interpreting experimental SANS data from vortex-state nanoparticles.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob

motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in supercooled liquids is crucial for glass transition theory.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare events.
result: Rare cage escapes are identified as the primary mechanism for structural relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems and challenge existing theories.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations operate in the saturated regime, but prior complexity theory only covered the dilute regime; this gap needed to be bridged.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of BosonSampling when the number of modes scales linearly with the number of photons, using techniques from permanent approximation and random matrix theory.
result: They show that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains hard for classical computers under plausible conjectures, extending the theoretical basis for quantum advantage.
conclusion: The results validate that current photonic experiments can achieve quantum advantage even in the saturated regime, reinforcing the promise of BosonSampling as a demonstration of quantum supremacy.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons

tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of quantum chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and can be detected via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum behavior of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential implications for condensed matter physics.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed to describe chiral solitons in spin chains, and their low-energy properties are analyzed.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: The findings suggest that chiral solitons are detectable via inelastic neutron scattering, providing a way to observe these excitations experimentally.

conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a viable tool for studying fermionic CFTs and can reveal emergent symmetries like supersymmetry.

result: Three distinct magnetic phases are discovered, and a design framework for materials that manipulate information via spin-based vortex lattices is established.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures, but its relevance to quantum information theory or information thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature

tldr: The paper studies topological Dirac magnons in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, focusing on the stability of magnon gaps near the Curie point.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of topological magnon gaps at finite temperatures is crucial for designing spintronic devices that operate above cryogenic temperatures.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions, likely involving spin-wave theory and self-consistent calculations, to compute the temperature dependence of magnon band structures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie temperature, contrary to expectations that thermal fluctuations would close them.
conclusion: The findings provide a roadmap for realizing robust topological spintronic devices based on van der Waals ferromagnets at practical temperatures.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?

method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks

result: The framework is demonstrated to accurately predict links across various network dynamics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
