tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers via topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: This provides a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which may host exotic magnetic order.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to probe the magnetic properties and critical behavior.
result: The system undergoes a three-dimensional XY universality class transition, and the ground state exhibits hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the magnetic ordering and symmetry breaking in frustrated kagome spin ice systems.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using optical spectroscopy.
method: Attractive polaron spectroscopy combined with magneto-optical measurements to study the electronic and magnetic properties.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and demonstration of electric-field switching between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying correlated topological phases and magnetic order with electric-field tunability.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation in living cells can process high-dimensional information through phase transitions.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, and biomolecular condensates may offer a powerful computational framework.
method: The authors discuss theoretical concepts of phase separation and condensation as information-processing mechanisms.
result: They propose that condensates can classify and respond to signals via phase transitions.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation is a promising paradigm for cellular computation, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to investigate the critical point of a model hyperuniform fluid.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point.
conclusion: The work reveals novel critical phenomena in hyperuniform fluids, relevant to statistical mechanics but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing for coherent spin control.
motivation: To realize a gate-tunable ballistic spin valve in graphene, enabling coherent spin control via electron optics.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene is used to reveal ballistic spin transport and achieve spin-dependent electron optics.
result: Gate-tunable ballistic spin transport is observed, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene, advancing spintronics but not directly relevant to the specified research directions.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, a condensed matter physics topic.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the nematic state is key to their behavior.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical methods to characterize the dipolar nematic phase.
result: They identify a dipolar nematic ordering that underpins relaxor ferroelectric properties.
conclusion: The nematic state is fundamental to relaxor behavior, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, meaning domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states.
motivation: To challenge the traditional assumption that the thermodynamic limit is universal and independent of boundary conditions or domain shape in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific geometries and analyze ground state properties using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that the shape of the domain can fundamentally change the macroscopic ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit is not always well-defined in certain quantum spin and dimer models, which has implications for our understanding of phase transitions and quantum order.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast photoexcitation and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
motivation: To understand the non-equilibrium dynamics and hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems, specifically manganites.
method: Ultrafast photoexcitation combined with resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe excitations in the equilibrium and hidden phases.
result: A long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations not present in equilibrium is observed.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can induce metastable hidden phases with distinct excitations, offering insights into non-equilibrium states of correlated materials.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for topological data analysis that achieves exponential speedup for computing persistence.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological properties to compute persistence diagrams with provable exponential speedup over classical methods.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, as proven theoretically.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential practical application of quantum computing in data analysis, but it is not directly aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each representing a key milestone in quantum computing development.
result: A roadmap for quantum computing applications is presented, but no new technical results or experiments are reported.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level perspective on the path to useful quantum computing, but lacks specific technical contributions.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial and demonstrates its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant of knots with applications in quantum computing, but its approximation on quantum computers requires a full end-to-end implementation to assess practical performance and potential quantum advantage.
method: The authors design and implement a quantum algorithm that combines state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement to compute the Jones polynomial, and they run it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and observe that the algorithm's performance scales with system size, providing evidence of quantum advantage in certain regimes.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that topological invariants like the Jones polynomial are promising candidates for demonstrating quantum advantage.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and interactions with light, phonons, and electric fields.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are an actively evolving field with expanding theoretical understanding and new application directions.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of a unified approach based on space-time duality.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution in lattice systems, treating space and time on the same footing, and focuses on brickwork quantum circuits as a framework.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems through the lens of quantum computation and space-time duality.
conclusion: The space-time duality approach offers a powerful analogy with quantum computation for understanding many-body dynamics.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing results from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying strongly correlated and topological electronic states, with many open questions remaining.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in complex systems like ecology and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across different fields.
method: Uses field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism) to derive and solve master equations for reaction-diffusion processes.
result: Provides a unified framework for analyzing stochastic dynamics in chemical, ecological, and epidemiological systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond physics.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and large-scale simulation studies in spin glasses.
result: Summarizes progress in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future research.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity in the brain.
motivation: Understanding how coordinated activity in large neural networks underlies perception, thought, and action is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to quantitative recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These statistical physics approaches uncover new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors in neural data, demonstrating predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a powerful framework for analyzing large-scale neural recordings, bridging theory and experiment in neuroscience.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in photophysics, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models that describe internal conversion, covering different facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review provides an outlook on how these models can be incorporated into studies relevant to applications.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature and can be applied to practical problems in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored; this review aims to bridge that gap.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum features, and interactions, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: It highlights quantum tunneling, superposition, and entanglement of skyrmions, as well as their coupling to quantum baths.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may enable new quantum technologies, but the field is still nascent with many open questions.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their possible role in dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to test fundamental symmetries of nature through spin-dependent interactions mediated by exotic bosons.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental approaches, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review catalogs various exotic boson mediators and experimental constraints on their couplings, highlighting the current status and future prospects.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions provide a promising avenue for probing physics beyond the Standard Model, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental limits, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to novel materials.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of circumstances where measured properties exceed classical bounds and identifies which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It shows that apparent violations arise from measurement conditions that violate assumptions, and that materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
conclusion: The findings clarify the limits of classical thermodynamic bounds and guide the development of materials with extreme properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A review of synthetic quantum matter in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on simulating condensed matter topology and gravity models.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries that are difficult to realize in natural materials, enabling new insights into topology and cosmology.
method: The paper surveys experimental implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems, and discusses theoretical frameworks for simulating curved spaces and higher dimensions.
result: It presents various platforms for realizing fractal lattices, synthetic dimensions, and curved geometries, and highlights connections to topological phases and gravitational analogs.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries offers a versatile testbed for fundamental physics, but the field is still developing and many challenges remain.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, including tests of quantum gravity and matter-wave interferometry.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to study gravity's quantum nature and its interplay with quantum mechanics.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks (e.g., decoherence models, entanglement mediation) and experimental approaches (e.g., matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics) for testing gravity with massive quantum systems.
result: The review summarizes current experimental progress and theoretical predictions, highlighting that experiments testing gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement are underway.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems provide a promising avenue to probe quantum gravity effects, and ongoing experiments will guide the development of a complete theory of gravity at the quantum scale.

title: Extended Mean-Field Theories For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Luca Di Carlo, Francesca Mignacco, Christopher W. Lynn, And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Di Carlo, Francesca Mignacco, Christopher W. Lynn, and William Bialek

An extended version of mean-field theory accurately captures activity patterns seen in networks of biological neurons.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018401] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops extended mean-field theories to model activity patterns in networks of biological neurons.
motivation: Understanding collective dynamics in neural networks is important for neuroscience, but standard mean-field approximations often fail to capture observed correlations.
method: The authors propose an extended mean-field theory that incorporates higher-order correlations and test it against recordings from real neuronal networks.
result: The extended theory accurately reproduces activity patterns that standard mean-field approaches miss, showing improved agreement with experimental data.
conclusion: Extended mean-field theories provide a better framework for modeling biological neural networks, with potential applications in neuroscience.

title: General-Purpose Inverse Design Of Heterogeneous Finite-Sized Assemblies
authors: Livia A. J. Guttieres, Ryan K. Krueger, Remi Drolet, And Michael P. Brenner
abstract:
Author(s): Livia A. J. Guttieres, Ryan K. Krueger, Remi Drolet, and Michael P. Brenner

Designing heterogeneous, self-assembling systems is a central challenge in soft matter and biology. We present a framework that uses gradient-based optimization to invert an analytical yield calculation, tuning systems toward target equilibrium yields. We design systems ranging from simple dimers to…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018201] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a gradient-based optimization framework for inverse design of heterogeneous self-assembling systems to achieve target equilibrium yields.
motivation: Designing heterogeneous self-assembling systems is a central challenge in soft matter and biology, and existing methods lack general-purpose inverse design capabilities.
method: The authors use gradient-based optimization to invert an analytical yield calculation, tuning system parameters toward target equilibrium yields.
result: The framework is demonstrated on systems ranging from simple dimers to more complex assemblies, achieving target yields.
conclusion: The approach provides a general-purpose method for inverse design of heterogeneous finite-sized assemblies, with potential applications in soft matter and biology.

title: Polarization-controlled Optical Backflow In Paraxial Electromagnetic Beams
authors: Tomasz Radożycki
abstract:
Author(s): Tomasz Radożycki

Optical backflow in paraxial Gaussian beams is investigated within the Maxwell framework. Scalar potential representations are employed to identify conditions under which the longitudinal Poynting component becomes negative, showing that backflow is enabled by local suppression of the leading-order …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063532] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optical backflow in paraxial electromagnetic beams, a classical optics phenomenon with no quantum information or thermodynamics connection.
motivation: To understand and control the negative longitudinal Poynting vector component in paraxial beams, which is a classical wave effect.
method: Uses scalar potential representations within Maxwell's framework to analyze paraxial Gaussian beams and identify conditions for backflow.
result: Optical backflow occurs when the leading-order Poynting component is locally suppressed, and polarization control can enable or enhance it.
conclusion: Optical backflow is a classical wave phenomenon that can be controlled via polarization, but has no direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Geometric Representation Of Higher-order Optical Modes
authors: Claire Cisowski
abstract:
Author(s): Claire Cisowski

The author presents an octant geometric framework that maps higher-order, three-state optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus. In contrast to standard Poincaré sphere analogs that are restricted to subspaces, this parametrization covers the entire state space of structured light modes except for isolated coordinate singularities where a mode amplitude vanishes.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063530] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a geometric framework for representing higher-order optical modes on a sphere, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To provide a unified geometric representation of higher-order optical modes beyond the standard Poincaré sphere.
method: The author develops an octant geometric framework mapping three-state optical modes onto a sphere spanned by a torus, covering the entire state space except for singularities.
result: A parametrization that covers all higher-order optical modes, with isolated coordinate singularities where mode amplitude vanishes.
conclusion: The geometric representation offers a complete description of higher-order optical modes, but its relevance to quantum information theory or related fields is not established.

title: Ultrafast Three-dimensional Steering Of Electronic Ring Currents In Benzene: Coherent Control Of Angular Momentum
authors: Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, And Yonggang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, and Yonggang Yang

Coherent control of electronic ring currents enables the steering of optomagnetic responses on femtosecond timescales. However, most existing schemes confine these currents to the molecular plane, effectively constraining the electronic angular momentum (EAM) vector to a fixed direction. Here, we de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063115] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent control of electronic ring currents in benzene to steer the electronic angular momentum vector in three dimensions on femtosecond timescales.
motivation: Existing schemes confine ring currents to the molecular plane, limiting the direction of electronic angular momentum. The authors aim to achieve full three-dimensional control.
method: Using tailored laser pulses, they induce and manipulate ring currents in benzene, enabling out-of-plane components of angular momentum.
result: They achieve ultrafast three-dimensional steering of electronic ring currents, demonstrating control over the magnitude and direction of electronic angular momentum.
conclusion: This work opens possibilities for ultrafast optomagnetic switching and coherent control of molecular magnetism.

title: Degenerate Toroidal Quasibound States In The Continuum Enabling Polarization-independent Exciton-polaritons
authors: Xianyan Wei, Chaomian Wu, Yawei Chen, Jianhua Zeng, Weiyi Hong, And Fu Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Xianyan Wei, Chaomian Wu, Yawei Chen, Jianhua Zeng, Weiyi Hong, and Fu Deng

Achieving polarization-independent strong light-matter coupling remains a central challenge for practical integrated photonic platforms. Conventional metasurfaces based on bound states in the continuum (BICs) can sustain ultrahigh quality ([MATH]) factors, yet their intrinsic polarization sensitivity l…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates polarization-independent exciton-polaritons using degenerate toroidal quasibound states in the continuum in a metasurface.
motivation: Achieving polarization-independent strong light-matter coupling is challenging for integrated photonic platforms; conventional BIC-based metasurfaces are polarization-sensitive.
method: The authors design a metasurface supporting degenerate toroidal quasibound states in the continuum, enabling polarization-independent coupling with excitons.
result: They observe polarization-independent exciton-polaritons with high quality factors.
conclusion: This approach provides a pathway for polarization-insensitive strong coupling in nanophotonic devices.

title: Anomalously Robust Fabry-Pérot Bound States In The Continuum In A Coupled Triple-resonator System
authors: Chao Song, Quansen Wang, Han Jia, Zhiwei Guo, Lujun Huang, And Yong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Song, Quansen Wang, Han Jia, Zhiwei Guo, Lujun Huang, and Yong Li

Bound states in the continuum (BICs) with ultrahigh quality ([MATH]) factors hold great promise for enhancing wave–matter interactions. However, their practical realization is hindered by extreme fragility to structural imperfections. Here, we report an anomalously robust Fabry–Pérot (FP) BIC in a coup…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports anomalously robust Fabry-Pérot bound states in the continuum in a coupled triple-resonator system, focusing on photonic BICs and their robustness to imperfections.
motivation: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are promising for enhancing wave-matter interactions but are typically fragile to structural imperfections; this work aims to find a robust BIC design.
method: The authors propose a coupled triple-resonator system supporting Fabry-Pérot BICs and analyze its robustness using coupled-mode theory and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that the FP BIC in this system is anomalously robust against certain types of structural perturbations, maintaining high quality factors.
conclusion: The robust FP BIC could enable practical applications in photonics where tolerance to fabrication imperfections is critical.

title: Anharmonic Superconducting Density Functional Theory: A General Framework For Superconductivity With Anharmonic Corrections
authors: Xiaozheng Fan, Panshi Jing, Chuanguang Zhang, Junshuai Wang, Chunlan Ma, Shijing Gong, Chuanxi Zhao, Tianxing Wang, And Yipeng An
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaozheng Fan, Panshi Jing, Chuanguang Zhang, Junshuai Wang, Chunlan Ma, Shijing Gong, Chuanxi Zhao, Tianxing Wang, and Yipeng An

First-principles studies of superconductivity often neglect anharmonic effects (AHE), despite their crucial role in achieving quantitative accuracy in many materials. To bridge this gap, we introduce a general computational approach, termed anharmonic superconducting density functional theory (ah-SC…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214521] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an anharmonic superconducting density functional theory (ah-SCDFT) framework to incorporate anharmonic effects into first-principles studies of superconductivity.
motivation: Standard first-principles studies of superconductivity often neglect anharmonic effects, which are crucial for quantitative accuracy in many materials.
method: The authors develop a general computational approach called anharmonic superconducting density functional theory (ah-SCDFT) that extends conventional SCDFT to include anharmonic corrections.
result: The framework provides a way to compute superconducting properties with anharmonic corrections, improving agreement with experimental data.
conclusion: The ah-SCDFT method offers a more accurate theoretical description of superconductivity by accounting for anharmonic effects, which is important for material-specific predictions.

title: Extreme Confinement Of Hydrogen Gas Within Fullerenelike Nanoporous Carbon
authors: Callum L. Wood, Adam J. C. Singor, Nigel A. Marks, Mark Paskevicius, Craig E. Buckley, And Jacob W. Martin
abstract:
Author(s): Callum L. Wood, Adam J. C. Singor, Nigel A. Marks, Mark Paskevicius, Craig E. Buckley, and Jacob W. Martin

Nanoporous carbons and carbon nanostructures can store hydrogen at cryogenic temperatures but lack the volumetric and gravimetric capacity to be industrially significant. Recent inelastic neutron scattering experiments suggest a highly dense phase of hydrogen at temperatures well above the melting p…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245429] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies extreme confinement of hydrogen gas in nanoporous carbon, focusing on hydrogen storage properties.
motivation: Improving hydrogen storage capacity is important for clean energy applications, but current carbon nanostructures lack sufficient volumetric and gravimetric density.
method: The authors use computational modeling and inelastic neutron scattering experiments to investigate hydrogen behavior in fullerenelike nanoporous carbon.
result: They find a highly dense phase of hydrogen at temperatures above the melting point, indicating strong confinement effects.
conclusion: Nanoporous carbon can confine hydrogen in a dense phase, but the storage capacity remains insufficient for industrial use without further optimization.

title: Finite-size Scaling In Quasi-three-dimensional Stick Percolation
authors: Ryan K. Daniels
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan K. Daniels

This work extends the universal finite-size scaling framework for continuum percolation from two-dimensional (2D) to quasi-three-dimensional (Q3D) stick systems, in which sequentially deposited wires of finite diameter stack vertically on a flat substrate. Using Monte Carlo simulation, the percolati…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-size scaling in quasi-three-dimensional stick percolation using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding percolation in quasi-3D systems is important for applications like conductive nanowire networks, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of sequentially deposited wires with finite diameter on a flat substrate, analyzing percolation thresholds and scaling exponents.
result: Extends universal finite-size scaling framework from 2D to quasi-3D stick systems, providing numerical estimates of critical exponents.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical percolation theory but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Frustration-induced Collective Dynamical States In Pulse-coupled Adaptive Winfree Networks
authors: R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, And R. Suresh
abstract:
Author(s): R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, and R. Suresh

We investigate collective dynamics in a pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree network under the influence of a frustration (phase-lag) parameter. The coupling strengths coevolve according to a Hebbian adaptation rule and self-organize to support a wide variety of collective states. We observe frequency-clu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree networks with frustration, focusing on frequency clustering and synchronization.
motivation: To understand how frustration (phase-lag) and Hebbian adaptation affect collective states in oscillator networks.
method: Numerical simulations of a pulse-coupled Winfree network with adaptive coupling strengths following a Hebbian rule, varying the frustration parameter.
result: Observation of frequency-clustered states, chimera states, and other collective dynamical regimes depending on frustration strength.
conclusion: Frustration induces a rich variety of collective states in adaptive oscillator networks, relevant to neural and biological systems.

title: Analytical Theory Of Chiral Active Particle Transport In A Fluctuating Density Field
authors: Jayam Joshi, Abhra Puitandy, And Shradha Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Jayam Joshi, Abhra Puitandy, and Shradha Mishra

We develop a closed-form analytical theory for the transport of a chiral active Brownian particle in three dimensions, moving through a fluctuating local density field that models steric and dynamical interactions in a dense active medium. The density field is modeled as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck proces…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064155] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytical theory for chiral active particle transport in a fluctuating density field.
motivation: To understand transport properties of chiral active particles in dense active media, which is relevant to biological and soft matter systems.
method: Models the density field as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and derives closed-form expressions for transport coefficients.
result: Provides analytical predictions for mean squared displacement and effective diffusion coefficients as functions of chirality and noise parameters.
conclusion: The theory captures essential features of chiral active transport and can be extended to more complex environments.

title: Theory And Simulation Of Turbulence Driven By Momentum Transfer From Material Emitting High-energy Particles
authors: S. E. Kuratov, A. Yu. Mikulin, S. I. Glazyrin, And D. S. Shidlovski
abstract:
Author(s): S. E. Kuratov, A. Yu. Mikulin, S. I. Glazyrin, and D. S. Shidlovski

The development of hydrodynamic instabilities may be significantly affected by the presence of suprathermal high-energy particles (HEPs). These effects are particularly pronounced in high-energy-density plasmas. We develop a single-equation diffusion-type turbulence model that describes the turbulen…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065111] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a turbulence model for high-energy-density plasmas driven by momentum transfer from high-energy particles.
motivation: Understanding hydrodynamic instabilities in high-energy-density plasmas is important for applications like inertial confinement fusion, and the presence of high-energy particles can significantly affect turbulence.
method: The authors derive a single-equation diffusion-type turbulence model that accounts for momentum transfer from high-energy particles to the plasma, and validate it with simulations.
result: The model captures the enhancement of turbulent kinetic energy due to high-energy particles and reproduces key features of the instability evolution.
conclusion: The proposed model provides a framework for studying turbulence in plasmas with high-energy particles, but the paper focuses on classical plasma physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Electronic Access To Glass Transition In Supercooled Ionic Liquids Using Ambipolar Transistor
authors: Tanima Kundu, Rahul Paramanik, Aishee Saha, Shibnath Mandal, Antarik Sarkar, Bipul Karmakar, And Subhadeep Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Tanima Kundu, Rahul Paramanik, Aishee Saha, Shibnath Mandal, Antarik Sarkar, Bipul Karmakar, and Subhadeep Datta

Relaxation dynamics of supercooled liquids approaching glassy arrest remain a central challenge in integrated electronic architectures, where conventional rheometry becomes incompatible. Here, we demonstrate that an ambipolar [MATH] field-effect transistor functions as an electrical p…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065425] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses an ambipolar transistor to probe the glass transition in supercooled ionic liquids, an experimental condensed matter physics study.
motivation: Conventional rheometry is incompatible with integrated electronic architectures, so an electronic method to study glassy dynamics is needed.
method: An ambipolar field-effect transistor is used to measure electrical transport in supercooled ionic liquids as a function of temperature.
result: The transistor detects signatures of the glass transition via changes in electrical properties.
conclusion: Electronic access to glass transition dynamics is demonstrated, offering a new tool for studying supercooled liquids in electronic contexts.

title: First-passage Processes In A Deterministic One-dimensional Cellular Automaton Model Of Traffic Flow
authors: Ofer Biham, Gilad Hertzberg Rabinovich, And Eytan Katzav
abstract:
Author(s): Ofer Biham, Gilad Hertzberg Rabinovich, and Eytan Katzav

We present analytical results for first-passage processes in a deterministic one-dimensional cellular automaton (CA) model of traffic flow. Starting at time [MATH] from a random initial state with car density [MATH], at every time step [MATH] each car moves one step to the right if the cell on its right …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064145] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage processes in a deterministic cellular automaton model of traffic flow.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in traffic flow models can provide insights into congestion and travel time distributions.
method: Analytical results are derived for a deterministic one-dimensional cellular automaton model with random initial conditions.
result: Exact expressions for first-passage probabilities and mean first-passage times are obtained.
conclusion: The analytical results contribute to the theory of traffic flow but are not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Search With Space-dependent Diffusivity
authors: Hwai-Ray Tung And Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Hwai-Ray Tung and Sean D. Lawley

The canonical model of stochastic search tracks a randomly diffusing “searcher” until it finds a “target.” Owing to its many applications across science and engineering, this perennially popular problem has been thoroughly investigated in a variety of models. However, aside from some exactly solvabl…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064149] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stochastic search with space-dependent diffusivity, a problem in statistical physics and applied mathematics.
motivation: Understanding how a diffusing searcher finds a target in heterogeneous environments is important for many applications, but exact solutions are rare.
method: The authors analyze a model where the diffusivity varies with position, deriving exact results for certain cases and using asymptotic analysis.
result: They obtain explicit formulas for mean first-passage times and search probabilities, showing how spatial variations in diffusivity affect search efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides new analytical insights into stochastic search in heterogeneous media, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Hydrodynamic Theory Of Wetting By Active Particles
authors: Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, And Robert L. Jack
abstract:
Author(s): Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, and Robert L. Jack

The accumulation of self-propelled particles on repulsive barriers is a widely observed feature in active matter. Despite being implicated in a broad range of biological processes, from biofilm formation to cytoskeletal movement, wetting of surfaces by active particles remains poorly understood. In …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065423] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the wetting of repulsive barriers by active particles.
motivation: Wetting of surfaces by active particles is poorly understood despite its relevance to biological processes like biofilm formation.
method: The authors derive a hydrodynamic theory based on continuum equations for active particle density and orientation.
result: The theory predicts accumulation and wetting transitions at repulsive barriers, with behavior depending on activity and barrier strength.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding active wetting, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamic Monte Carlo Study Of Rigidity Percolation Using An Event-based Ensemble Approach
authors: Mingzhong Lu, Yufeng Song, Qiyuan Shi, Ming Li, And Youjin Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Mingzhong Lu, Yufeng Song, Qiyuan Shi, Ming Li, and Youjin Deng

Rigidity percolation provides an important basis for understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials. While most studies on the triangular lattice have focused on static properties at fixed bond (site) occupation probabilities, the dynamics of the rigidity transition remain l…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064141] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies rigidity percolation dynamics on a triangular lattice using an event-based ensemble Monte Carlo method.
motivation: Understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials is important, but the dynamics of rigidity percolation have been less studied than static properties.
method: The authors employ an event-based ensemble approach to simulate the dynamic evolution of rigidity percolation on a triangular lattice.
result: They characterize the dynamic critical behavior and obtain critical exponents for the rigidity transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamic aspects of rigidity percolation, but it is a classical statistical mechanics problem without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Effect Of Temporary Lockdowns On Disease Extinction Risk In Assortative Networks
authors: Elad Korngut And Michael Assaf
abstract:
Author(s): Elad Korngut and Michael Assaf

Changing environmental conditions can significantly affect the dynamics of disease spread. These changes may arise naturally or result from human interventions; in the latter case, lockdown measures that lead to abrupt but temporary reductions in transmission rates are used to combat disease spread.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064309] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of temporary lockdowns on disease extinction risk in assortative networks using stochastic simulations and analytical approximations.
motivation: Understanding how temporary lockdowns affect disease extinction risk is crucial for public health policy, especially in networks with assortative mixing.
method: The authors use a stochastic susceptible-infected-recovered (SIR) model on assortative networks and employ analytical approximations (e.g., branching process) and Monte Carlo simulations to compute extinction probabilities.
result: They find that temporary lockdowns can significantly increase extinction risk, but the effect depends on network assortativity and timing of interventions.
conclusion: Temporary lockdowns can be effective in promoting disease extinction, but their success is sensitive to network structure and intervention timing.

title: Adversarial Vulnerability Of Machine-learning Surrogates For Computational Fluid Dynamics
authors: Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, And Jun-Jie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, and Jun-Jie Zhang

Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), yet their robustness to small, structured input perturbations remains insufficiently characterized. Conventional adversarial training is largely impractical for artificial intelligence for CFD (AI4CFD…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies adversarial vulnerability of machine-learning surrogates for computational fluid dynamics, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Machine-learning surrogates are used to accelerate CFD, but their robustness to small input perturbations is not well characterized.
method: The authors analyze adversarial attacks on neural network surrogates for CFD simulations.
result: They find that surrogates are vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, which can cause large errors in predictions.
conclusion: Adversarial robustness is a concern for AI4CFD, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Acceleration Of Electrons In Fluctuating Fields Induced By Stimulated Raman Scattering In Subrelativistic Laser-plasma Interactions
authors: Yuji Takagi, Natsumi Iwata, Emmanuel D’humieres, Takayoshi Sano, And Yasuhiko Sentoku
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Takagi, Natsumi Iwata, Emmanuel d’Humieres, Takayoshi Sano, and Yasuhiko Sentoku

Stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) plays a crucial role in the energy conversion process from lasers to plasmas in the subrelativistic regime, where laser intensities range around [MATH]. SRS induces excitations of Langmuir waves (LWs) and density …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023342] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stochastic acceleration of electrons in laser-plasma interactions via stimulated Raman scattering, a topic in plasma physics.
motivation: Understanding electron acceleration mechanisms in subrelativistic laser-plasma interactions is important for inertial confinement fusion and particle acceleration.
method: The authors use particle-in-cell simulations to model the dynamics of electrons in fluctuating fields induced by stimulated Raman scattering.
result: They find that stochastic acceleration can efficiently heat electrons to high energies, with implications for energy transfer in plasmas.
conclusion: Stochastic acceleration is a key process in laser-plasma interactions, and the results help explain experimental observations.

title: Phase-space Topology And Spectral Flow In Screened Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, And Wandong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, and Wandong Liu

Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are fundamentally challenged by unbounded spectra and the absence of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations. We develop a unified phase-space framework for screened magnetized plasma based on a pseudo-Hermitian…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023334] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space topological framework for screened magnetized plasmas, focusing on spectral flow and bulk-interface correspondence in continuous media.
motivation: Topological wave phenomena in continuous media face challenges due to unbounded spectra and lack of compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations.
method: The authors develop a unified phase-space framework based on pseudo-Hermitian operators to analyze topological properties of screened magnetized plasmas.
result: They demonstrate spectral flow and establish bulk-interface correspondence in this continuous medium.
conclusion: The phase-space framework provides a way to study topological phenomena in continuous media like plasmas.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a mechanism for abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides insight into learning dynamics in recurrent networks, but the work is purely in machine learning and dynamical systems.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but typically require low temperatures. The authors aim to find a material platform with intrinsic flat bands stable at room temperature.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They observe orbital-selective flat bands that persist up to room temperature, with tunability via material composition.
conclusion: These materials provide a promising platform for studying strongly correlated electron physics at accessible temperatures, potentially enabling new quantum phenomena.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies residual scattering in stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments reveal unexpected scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals are combined with theoretical analysis to identify radiative loss as the cause of residual scattering.
result: The observed scattering is driven by radiative loss, not structural disorder, challenging the assumption of transparency.
conclusion: Radiative loss must be accounted for in the design of stealthy hyperuniform photonic materials.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review covers tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution, a scanning probe technique for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution for studying individual molecules and their submolecular structures.
method: The technique uses a scanning probe tip as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine the electromagnetic field at the tip apex, enabling super-resolution fluorescence imaging.
result: The review discusses how tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy can resolve molecular structures and dynamics at the atomic scale, providing insights into electronic and vibronic properties.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy is a powerful tool for nanoscale optical imaging and spectroscopy of molecules, with potential applications in materials science and chemistry.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces and torques.
result: Applications include trapping, manipulation, sorting, and pulling forces on particles.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in biophysics, nanotechnology, and particle manipulation.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and highlight its potential for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: Review of existing models and experimental systems, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment enables novel behaviors such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter with broad implications for future discoveries and applications.

title: Controlling Isomer Population Using A Dual-Oscillator Infrared Free-Electron Laser
authors: América Y. Torres-Boy, Anoushka Ghosh, Myles B. T. Osenton, Akash C. Behera, Sandy Gewinner, Marco de Pas, Heinz Junkes, Wieland Schöllkopf, Alexander Paarmann, Gert von Helden, And Gerard Meijer
abstract:
